1 Welcome & overview BrewDesk is a till for your shop. It takes orders and money for cafes, restaurants, bars, bakeries, and salons. It works on a laptop or a tablet you already have. It even keeps working when the internet stops. This page is a quick look around. It takes about one minute to read. Reports & daily insights ① Total Sales and the other total cards · ② Staff Sales and Attendance Log tabs (locked on the Starter plan) · ③ Revenue Trends chart Is this for you? If you sell things and take money, BrewDesk is for you. You do not need to be good with computers. You do not need a tech helper.

2 Quick start This is the quickest way to make your very first sale. You can do it in about five minutes. Just follow each tiny step. Open a web browser and go to brewdesk.io. Type your email and a password to sign up. You do not need a credit card. Pick what kind of shop you have. Choose cafe, restaurant, bar, salon, spa, or bakery. BrewDesk sets things up to match. Tap the AI menu builder button. This makes a starter menu for you in seconds. (Or you can type a few items yourself.) Look for the order screen. Tap an item to add it to the order. Tap Cash to finish the sale right away. A "Sale complete" message appears. That's it — your first sale is done! Later, when you want to take cards, you can link your own Stripe account. (We show you how in Getting paid .) Don't worry if you get something wrong. You can change anything later in Settings . Nothing here is final. Show this off Five minutes, nothing to install, no lessons needed. Most other tills make you book a setup call. BrewDesk lets you start selling before your coffee gets cold.

First-time setup (the 7 steps) When you first sign up, a friendly wizard walks you through a few simple steps. Here is what it asks, in order. Just tap your way through. If you pick Quick mode at the top left, the Service Mode and Add-ons steps are skipped; Full mode goes through all 7 steps below. Business Type — pick what kind of shop you have: cafe, restaurant, bar, salon, spa, or bakery. Store Info — type your store name, pick your country or region, and say how many registers (tills) you have. Service Mode — choose Counter (people order at the counter) or Table service (people order at their table). Add-ons — switch on the extra features you want. You can change these later, so don't worry. Plan — pick Starter (free), Pro , or Business . Pro and Business come with a 1-month free trial, and you don't need a credit card to start. Menu — start from a ready-made template, let the AI build it for you, or add items yourself. (More about the AI menu builder in Building your menu .) Done — the "Setup complete!" screen sums up your choices. To take cards, tap Connect Stripe here — or connect later in Settings › Payments . Finally tap Start using BrewDesk . Only if you pick the Staff add-on , one extra step — Owner PIN — appears after the Menu step (a 4-digit PIN; you can skip it). When it shows, the wizard has 8 steps instead of 7. That's it! You'll just confirm a quick tax note, and you're ready to sell. The setup wizard ① Quick or Full mode · ② The 7 steps down the side (Business Type → Store Info → Service Mode → Add-ons → Plan → Menu → Done) · ③ Progress bar · ④ "Start using BrewDesk" when you're finished (if you pick the Staff add-on, an "Owner PIN" step is added between Menu and Done) The whole thing takes about 5 minutes. And remember — you can change anything later in Settings . When you're ready, switch from practice to real trading in Going live .

3 Setting up your store Now let's fill in the basics about your shop. You only do this once. Take it slow — one box at a time. Store Info ① Store name · ② Business type · ③ Logo / branding · ④ Save Hours & Closures ① Operating days · ② Shift hours bar · ③ Add Shift · ④ Services allowed in this shift (Reservations / Waitlist / QR) Tap Settings (the gear icon) near the bottom of the left sidebar. Tap Store Info . Store Info — lower part ① State · city · address · ZIP · ② Timezone · ③ App Language · ④ Save Type your shop's name, address, and the money you use (like dollars or pounds). Check your business type is right (cafe, restaurant, and so on). This sets up tables, staff, and PIN logins for you. Open Hours & Closures and type the times your shop is open. These times tell BrewDesk when people can book a table, join the line, and order by phone. Open the tax setting. BrewDesk adds the right tax for you, so you don't have to do the math. Add your receipt bits, like your logo and a thank-you message at the bottom. Tap Save . Your shop is now set up. Tip: Tax is the extra bit of money the government asks for on a sale. BrewDesk works it out for you — you just turn it on. Time zone is worth a second look. If the device you're on is in a different time zone from your store setting, a banner appears at the top: "This device's time zone (…) is different from your store's setting (…). Sales days and closing reports follow the store setting, so please make sure it is correct." Tap Check time zone to jump straight to the setting. It only appears when the clocks really differ, so it won't nag you for two cities that share a time. On your main till the wording is stronger — that's the device your business day is measured from. Good to know: some countries have e-invoicing or fiscal-record rules we don't support yet, so they aren't offered. If you pick one and save, you'll see "This country is not supported." If your country isn't on the list, get in touch with support.

Set your tax Tax is the extra bit of money the government asks for on a sale. You only set this up once, and then BrewDesk adds it for you on every sale. Let's get your rate right. Where to find it Tap Settings in the left sidebar, then open Settings › Tax & Service . BrewDesk can suggest a rate for your area, but you confirm it. Tap Refresh Now to fetch a suggested rate, or just type your own. Type your rate in the rate box on the tax row (the number box with a % beside it, to the right of the name box that says Tax ) — for example, type 8 for 8%. Choose how tax shows. Tax Inclusive Pricing ON means tax is already inside the price you show. OFF means tax is added on top at checkout. Optional: add a Service Charge (a % or a fixed amount), and choose whether the service charge is taxed. Tap Save . A live receipt preview on the right shows a sample calculation, so you can check it looks right. A note reminds you that tax rates are suggestions — confirm yours with your tax advisor. Not sure which rate to pick? Don't worry. Tap Refresh Now for a suggestion to start with, then check it with your tax advisor or accountant. You can change it any time. Tax-inclusive store? Receipts now label the tax line "Tax (incl.)" when Tax Inclusive Pricing is ON — so customers can see the tax is already built into the price, not added on top. "Tax Amount Rounding" — renamed, and now it says what it does. The setting that used to be called "Tax Rounding Rule" is now Tax Amount Rounding : "Sets how the tax amount is reduced to the currency's smallest unit — cents in most currencies, whole yen or won where the currency has no decimals. Applies to every order, whatever the customer pays with." The choices are the same four — "Standard (0.005 → Round Up)" , Always Round Up , Always Round Down , No Rounding . Underneath, BrewDesk now shows the usual rule for your country as a reference: "Country default for … : … . Your setting is what the POS uses." — a reference only; your choice wins. Two small chips next to it say where you stand at a glance: "prices include tax" or "tax added at checkout" , and "service charge is taxed" or "service charge is not taxed" . Nothing about your existing tax numbers changed with this rename. Don't mix this up with cash rounding. Tax Amount Rounding is about the tax figure and applies to every sale. Matching the final total to a coin you actually have — the 1-cent piece nobody carries — is a separate setting under Settings › Payments , and it only ever touches cash. See Cash payment rounding . Different items, different tax? Use Tax types Some places tax things differently — for example, plain groceries may have no tax while a hot drink does. If that's you, BrewDesk can keep a few tax types and you pick the right one for each item. If every item in your shop uses the same rate, you can skip this — nothing changes for you. Where to find it Open Settings › Tax & Service and look for the Tax types card. It shows up for shops in places that need it (Canada, for example), and for some US shops that turn it on. Tax & Service — taxes and tax types ① Tax name box (default Tax ) and rate box (% on the right) · ② Add tax · ③ Add tax type · ④ Save Tax & Service ① Current tax rate · ② Tax box with % — type your rate · ③ Save · ④ Live receipt preview Tap Set up tax types . BrewDesk fills in the usual taxes for your region. If yours look different, a yellow note says "These taxes don't match the standard for your region." — tap Use regional standard to fix them in one tap. Under Taxes , each tax has a Tax name and a Tax rate (%) . Tap Add tax to add another one. This is the only place a tax rate is set. Under Tax types , tap Add tax type , give it a Tax type name , and tick the "Taxes that apply" . Choose No tax (exempt) for things that carry no tax at all. One type is marked Default . It's used for any item that has no tax type of its own, and for the service charge. Go to Manage › Menu Items in the left sidebar. On a category, pick "Tax type for this category" . On an item, pick Tax type . Leave an item on Follow category unless it is taxed differently. BrewDesk may suggest one for you. If an item looks like the others in its category, you'll see "Suggested: … — not confirmed" . Nothing changes until you tap "Use this" . Lower tax on small amounts. Some places charge less tax when the price is small — Ontario, for example, rebates part of the tax on prepared food and drinks of $4 or less. Turn on Use an amount condition under Lower tax below an amount , pick the two taxes it switches between, and choose whether to measure the Order total or "Each item's unit price" . A short sentence below it tells you in plain words what the rule will do. Good to know: receipts and reports show each tax on its own line, so two taxes can't share the same name — BrewDesk asks you to rename one. A few places (Massachusetts and Rhode Island) tax only the part above a limit; the amount condition can't copy that, so a warning appears there. Always check your setup with your tax advisor.

Holidays & special days Mark the days you're closed, and BrewDesk stops customers from booking a table, joining the queue, or ordering from their phone on that day. Public holidays, staff training, a sudden day off — you set them all here. Where to find it Open Settings › Hours & Closures and look for Holidays & Special Days lower down the page. You can use it even without the Reservations add-on turned on. The calendar sits on the left; the list of closures for the month you're viewing sits on the right. Add a closure ① One day / Date range · ② Closed all day switch · ③ Services to close · ④ Add Tap "+ Add" above the list, tap a date on the calendar, or tap an existing entry in the list — a pop-up opens. Pick the date(s). Choose One day for a single date, or Date range to close a stretch of days at once (up to 31) — handy for multi-day holidays. Turn on Closed all day . Once it's on, choose what stops under Services to close — reservations, waitlist, online & QR ordering. You can close just one and leave the rest open. Type a short Label like "Christmas" or "Staff training". Whatever you write in Message shown to guests is what your customers will see. Tap Save . It shows up on the calendar and in the list right away. Leaving "Closed all day" off blocks saving. Right now you can only register a closure — custom opening hours for a single day are marked "Coming soon" and can't be saved yet. The old Limited Capacity option (per-day capacity limits) is also gone; use the service checkboxes in step 3 instead if you only want to close some services. Already have bookings that day? When you save a single day, a pop-up lets you choose one of three things — "Leave as is" , Notify only (keep the bookings, just send a closure notice), or Cancel all (cancel every booking and tell the guests). Saving a closure never deletes bookings on its own; it only does what you pick. For a date range , this pop-up doesn't appear — after saving, open each day from the list to notify or cancel. You can still fix last month's entries. Both the calendar and the list can move to previous months, so you can edit or delete an old closure. To remove one, tap the delete icon on its row in the list. A weekday you close every week isn't set here — just switch that day off in the business days row at the top of the same screen, and it repeats automatically. Those show up in the list with a separate Regular badge. Repeat every year repeats on the solar calendar date. Lunar holidays (like Lunar New Year) land on a different date each year, so it's safer to mark those by hand every year. Also note: a yearly repeat does block bookings on that date, but the guest booking calendar doesn't grey it out yet — guests only see the closure notice after they pick that date. Show this off Mark the day off once, and everything closes together. Your booking page, your queue and your customers' phone ordering all shut for that day — no running around switching each one off, and multi-day holidays can be registered in one go.

t: See your service status at a glance
b: See your service status at a glance Can customers book right now? Join the queue? Order from their phone? One set of buttons tells you straight away — so you know before a customer tells you something isn't working. Where to find it Tap Tables in the left sidebar to open the Table Map screen — the toolbar at the top has three buttons: Online Orders , Reservations and Waitlist . Nothing to switch on — they're always there. (These used to be small badges in the top bar; they now live as bigger buttons on the Table Map.) The button colour tells you the state — coloured means it's running normally, grey means you've turned it off, grey with a clock means it's paused for now, and grey with a lock means it's blocked by something like your plan or payment setup. Tap a button to open "What customers can use right now" . It tells you why something is closed — for example "Closed today", "Outside business hours", "Main POS is offline", "Requires the {plan} plan", "Payment setup required", or "Monthly order limit reached". Need to stop taking something for a bit? Tap "Pause for today…" at the bottom. Pick the service and how long — 20 minutes , 60 minutes , Until close today (it reopens by itself at your next opening), or Until I turn it back on . You can also pause and resume from the side panel. Open the Online Orders, Reservations, or Waitlist side panel and there's a Pause / Resume button at the bottom — it opens the same window as the Table Map buttons. Perfect when the kitchen is slammed. Pause online orders for "20 minutes" and keep serving the people in front of you while you catch up. It reopens on its own. Who can change it. Only the owner and managers can pause a service — anyone else gets a "you don't have permission" note. Everyone can still see the status. If the Reservations add-on is off , the Reservations button won't show at all — turn the add-on back on to see it again. Good to know: the reason wording also shows on your customers' screen, so they aren't left wondering why they can't order.
4 Building your menu Your menu is the list of things you sell. It fills up the order screen. Let's add your items and sort them into groups.

Categories & items Add a menu item ① Add Item · ② Item details (name, price, category, photo) · ③ AI Generate a photo · ④ Add Category Tap Manage › Menu Items in the left sidebar. Top-right you'll see the buttons AI Fill , Export , Import , "Move" and Add Item ; Add Category sits at the far left of the category tab row. Category panel ① Add Category · ② Type the category name · ③ Sales channels (POS · In-Store QR · Online) · ④ Attach add-on groups · ⑤ Save Make a category first. Tap Add Category , type a name like "Coffee", and save. (You need at least one category before Add Item works.) Fill in the item ① Add Item · ② Item Name · ③ Category · ④ Price ($) · ⑤ Save Tap Add Item . A side panel opens. Fill in: Item Name, Description (optional), Category, Price, and Stock Status (the "In Stock" toggle). Add an item photo ① Light / Dark / Scene (photo background style) · ② Upload your own photo · ③ AI Generate · ④ Save Add a photo. Tap Upload to use your own picture, or AI Generate to make one. Tap Save . The item shows up in its category. What is a category? It is just a group, like a folder. It keeps your menu tidy so items are easy to find.

Option groups & presets Create an add-on group ① Add Group · ② Required (customer must pick one) · ③ Choice names and extra prices (e.g. Oat milk 0.5) · ④ Add Choice · ⑤ Save Attach the group to an item ① Pick the item (Caffè Latte) · ② The group now listed under Addon Groups — REQ means required · ③ Save Want to give choices? Attach option groups (like milk or size) in the item panel. You build groups with Add Group , pick a type (Single / Multi / Quantity), and add choices with prices. Ready-made option groups. Don't want to build groups from scratch? In the item panel tap Add from Presets to open the Preset Library — ready-made groups like Milk , Size , Temperature , and Sweetness for cafes, or Spice , Protein , and Sides for restaurants. Tap a card to add the whole group to your menu; it shows an Added badge once it's in.

AI photos & AI Fill AI Fill — the whole menu at once ① Which items · ② What to make · ③ Background style · ④ Generate Want a nicer photo? In the item panel, pick a background style (Light / Dark / Scene), then tap AI Generate . It makes 3 photos — tap the one you like. Do the whole menu at once with "AI Fill". Tap AI Fill , pick which items (All items / Missing image only / Specific category), pick what to make (Image + Description / Image only / Description only), pick a background style (Light — Pure white studio / Dark — Dark charcoal / Scene — Café bokeh), then tap Generate for N items . Review the results and tap Apply . Show this off The AI can write your whole menu for you — and even make item photos. So you start with a full menu in seconds, not a blank screen.

Import & export Export ① Export tab · ② Tick what to include (Menu Items, Addon Groups, …) · ③ Save to Drive · ④ Download Import ① Import tab · ② Choose the backup file · ③ Import AI Import — any file ① AI Import tab · ② Choose file (spreadsheet, CSV, PDF or a photo of a menu) Already have a menu in a spreadsheet? Tap Import to bring it all in at once. Tap Export to download your menu as a spreadsheet. Move — reorder ① Drag a category chip by its ⋮⋮ handle · ② Drag an item by its handle · ③ Save

5 Staff quick start A one-page guide for anyone running the till for the first time. It follows a shift from clock-in to clock-out. Each step is kept short — tap the links when you want the full story. Get these from the owner first ① A staff account in your name and a 4-digit PIN ( Add a staff member ) · ② whether this store takes orders at the counter or at tables · ③ which manager to call for refunds or bigger discounts. Keep your PIN to yourself — the activity log records actions under your name. When you arrive Lock screen ① Select Profile screen · ② Pick a name, then enter the PIN Clock in — tap the coloured role chip in the top bar to open the Time Clock panel. Tap In next to your name and enter your 4-digit PIN. If "Take the POS?" appears, choose Yes when you are the one running this till. (Used in stores with the Staff add-on — Staff & permissions .) PIN sign-in & Idle Lock — in stores that use Idle Lock , a till left alone for a while switches to the Select Profile lock screen. Tap your name and enter your PIN to carry on. The default PIN 0000 can't be used to sign in, so if yours is still 0000, ask the owner for a new one ( Permissions, manager PIN & role chip , Forgot a PIN? ). Serving customers Take the order — at the counter, tap items into the order and tap Pay Now . At tables, tap the guest's table on the table map first. If a guest steps away, park the order with Hold ( Taking orders , Hold an order ). Checkout — taking cash ① Cash · ② Amount received · ③ Change to Return · ④ Pay with … — Cash Take payment — tap Cash and enter the amount handed over; the change is shown. Tap Card when a card reader is connected, or a card-brand button (Record Only) when the card was taken on a separate terminal. Don't close the payment screen while the reader is still approving a card. When several people share a bill, use Split ( Getting paid , Split the bill ). Quick discount or free item — tap an item in the cart for the Discount and Free buttons; for the whole order, tap Disc at the bottom. Enter an amount or %, pick a reason chip (Friend · Apology · Staff · Tasting · Mistake) and tap Done ( Quick discount or free item ). Who can refund? — out of the box, the owner and managers can refund; a staff member needs a manager (or the owner) to approve with a PIN. The owner may have changed this in the permissions table, so when a customer asks for a refund, call a manager. Refunds are done from Manage › Payment History by opening the order ( Refunds , permissions ). When something goes wrong Working offline ① The orange bar means you're offline — keep taking orders; they save on the device and sync when you're back online The internet drops — an orange bar appears at the top. Keep taking orders as usual: they are saved on the device and upload by themselves when the connection returns. Only connected card-reader payments , sending messages and new bookings have to wait for the internet ( Working offline , What needs the internet ). A staff-ordering tablet says "Not sent to the kitchen" — check the main till is on and on the same store Wi-Fi, then tap Try again . Tap Entered on Main POS only if you actually typed the order in on the main till ( Staff Ordering ). Before you leave Tidy up open orders — settle anything on Hold or still unpaid, or tell a manager about it. Unpaid orders block closing the day ( Late orders & missed days ). The cash drawer and closing the day belong to managers and the owner — the Cash Drawer menu only appears for them. If you were holding the drawer, count it and hand it over to a manager ( Cash drawer , Reports & closing the day ). Clock out — tap the role chip, tap Out next to your name in the Time Clock and enter your PIN. If "Who takes over?" appears, pick the next person on the till or Return to Owner . Unfamiliar screen? Don't just tap through it. Most messages say exactly what to do next. If you are still stuck, call a manager or check Troubleshooting & support .

6 Taking orders This is the main job: taking an order. It works a little differently for counter shops and for table shops. Find your way below. Order screen ① Menu — tap items to add · ② Current order · ③ Hold (park the order for later) · ④ Pay Now An order with items ① Item card (quantity badge) · ② Items in Current Order · ③ Hold · ④ Disc · ⑤ Pay Now Option popup ① Dine-in / Takeaway · ② Milk Choice — REQUIRED · ③ Choices (extra price shown) · ④ Quantity · ⑤ Add to Order If you serve at a counter: tap each item the customer wants. It goes into the order on the side of the screen. Tap the same item again to add more of it. The number goes up. When the order is done, tap Pay Now to take the money. After tapping a table ① Guests + / − · ② Start Order If you serve at tables: open the table map (a picture of your floor). Tap the table where the customer is sitting. This starts their order. Add their items the same way — tap each one. Need a special note for the kitchen? Tap the item, then add an item note , like "extra hot" or "no ice". Need to stop and come back later? Tap Hold . The order is saved. You can open it again any time (see "Hold an order" below). Takeaway? A takeaway order (food to carry out) is kept separate from table orders, so they never get mixed up.

Hold an order Park an order for later. Sometimes you can't finish an order right away — a customer steps away, or a new person walks up. Hold lets you park the order and come back to it. Nothing is charged, and nothing is lost. Look at the bottom of the order panel. You'll see the Hold button, right next to Disc (discount). Hold Orders panel ① Save to Hold · ② Saved Held Orders list Tap Hold . The order is parked without charging anyone. The screen clears so you can serve the next person. At a table, the held order stays attached to that table — so it's easy to find again. A held order ① Held order card — tap to reopen · ② Close (X) To get it back, open the held-orders list and tap the order to resume it. The order comes back just as you left it. Add more items if you like, then carry on to Pay Now . When should I use Hold? Use it when a customer steps away to grab something, or when you need to start someone else's order first. The parked order waits safely until you're ready — nothing is lost.

Build your table map If you serve at tables, the table map is a little picture of your room. You tap a table to start that table's order. You set it up once. Here's how to draw it. Where to turn it on Table service is on by default for Restaurant and Bar business types. Otherwise turn it on in Settings › Add-ons › Tables (flip the switch). The table map only shows when table service is on. Before you begin: make sure table service is on (see the box above). Set up tables (Settings › Add-ons › Tables) ① The Settings menu — every setting lives here · ② Choose Counter Mode or Table Mode Table map ① A table — tap to start a dine-in order · ② Reservations button · ③ Scheduler tab. The green sidebar on the left is your main menu. Edit a table ① Tap a table on the map · ② Name & seats · ③ Shape, size & color · ④ Done Open the Table Map — tap Tables in the left sidebar. (It only appears when table service is on.) Tap the gear icon next to the Table Map tab at the top ( Edit Layout ) to enter the editor. If you have no tables yet, you can also tap the Open Editor button in the middle of the screen. This is where you build your room. In the toolbar at the top, tap the shape you want to add — Round , Square , Rect or Wall , plus Counter , Door and WC . A new table (or fixture) appears. Tap the table you added and an edit panel opens on the right. Set its Name (like "T1" or "Patio 3"), number of Seats , Shape , Size and Color , then tap Done . You'll see the table change as you pick. Drag the table to where it really sits in your room. Repeat for every table you have. When you're done, tap the Table Map (back) button at the top left to return to the map. Now you can tap a table to start a dine-in order. Don't fuss over it. The map doesn't have to be perfect. As long as you can tell your tables apart, you're good. You can move tables around any time.

Move & merge tables Move and merge by drag & drop. Guests change their minds. Someone wants to move to the patio, or two tables decide to pay together. On the Table Map you can pick up a table's whole order and drop it somewhere else — nothing gets re-typed. Where to find it It's built right into the Table Map . It works any time Table service is on — there's nothing to switch on. Move an order to an empty table Press and hold a busy table for a moment until it lifts up, then drag it onto an empty table and let go. A little box asks "Move T1 to T3?" — tap Move . The whole order jumps to the new table, and the old table becomes empty. The table's name doesn't change. Merge two busy tables into one bill Merge tables ① Title "Move T1 onto T2?" — T1 dropped onto T2 · ② Tap "Merge" to combine both into one bill · ③ "Cancel" to back out. Dropping onto an empty table shows a simpler "Move" instead. Press and hold a busy table, then drag it onto another busy table. The box title now reads "Move T1 onto T2?" , the Move option is greyed out ("Move unavailable"), and a Merge card shows — "T1 + T2 into one order on T2." Tap it. Both orders become a single bill on the table you dropped onto, and the other table empties. Dropped it on the wrong table? An Undo button pops up for about 6 seconds right after a move or merge — tap it to put everything back the way it was. (Undo can't reverse a merge once new items were added or money was taken on the combined bill.) Show this off Move a whole party with one finger. Most tills make you void the order and ring it all again just to change tables. BrewDesk simply slides it over — and a 6-second Undo means a slip of the finger never costs you a sale. Good to know: dropping onto a reserved table warns you first. A merged bill keeps the main table's discounts, and every table is still one clean order. A table looks busy but has no order? Sometimes a table gets opened — for example by a QR scan — but no order is placed, so it stays marked as occupied. Tap that table on the map and BrewDesk offers to clear it (tidy it back to empty) or open a new order. Clearing only works when there's no order and no payment on the table, so you can never lose a real sale.

7 Getting paid Now the fun part — getting paid. You can take cash today. You can take cards as soon as you link your own Stripe account. BrewDesk never adds a fee on top of your card sales. Payment screen ① Total due / Remaining · ② Payment methods — Cash, card brands (Visa, MasterCard, Amex), Card (External), Voucher (the card ones say Record Only), with the Full Pay / Split Pay toggle above · ③ Keypad (enter cash received) · ④ "Pay with…" to finish Finish the order, then tap Pay Now . BrewDesk shows you the change to give back. To take a card: if a card reader (Stripe terminal) is connected, tap Card . If not, you'll see card-brand buttons such as Visa , MasterCard and Amex , plus Card (External) — these just record a card payment you took on a separate terminal ( Record Only ). (Reader payments need your Stripe account linked first — see the next step.) To take cards, link your own Stripe account in Settings › Payments . It's free to connect. On the same screen you can switch the Cash , Card (Record Only) and Voucher payment methods on or off. The Full Pay / Split Pay toggle at the top of the checkout screen: Full Pay (the default) takes the whole amount with one method; Split Pay is for one person paying part by cash and part by card. Need to split one bill between people? Tap the Split button at the bottom right of the order screen. You can split it evenly or by item — and each share can have its own tip. See Split the bill just below. Payment complete ① Receipt preview · ② Change to Return · ③ Email Receipt / Send Receipt (Reprint prints again) · ④ Start New Order Show this off BrewDesk adds 0% on your card sales, on every plan. Your money goes straight to your own Stripe account. BrewDesk never sits in the middle and never takes a slice. * * You pay Stripe's standard rate directly to them — BrewDesk adds 0% on top. Who gets the tip? When a tip is added, BrewDesk asks you to choose which staff member earned it — tap Assign staff and pick a name. If just one server is on that table, they're picked for you automatically. If no one is chosen, the tip is saved under Store Manager so it's never lost. Recording a card by hand? If you take cards on a separate terminal that isn't connected to BrewDesk, the card brands — Visa , Mastercard , Amex and so on — now sit right next to Cash on the payment screen. One tap records both that it was a card and which brand, with no extra step. The payment screen won't close while the card reader is working. If you tap the X while a connected card reader is still charging the card, the screen stays put and tells you why: Card payment in progress — "The reader is still charging this card. Wait until it finishes — closing now could take the money without recording it on the order." It's a few seconds, and it's the difference between the money being on the order and the money just being gone. The X frees itself the moment the reader finishes, whether the card went through or not.

Split the bill When a table wants to pay separately, BrewDesk splits the bill for you. There are two easy ways: split it evenly between people, or split it by item so each person pays for what they had. Every share can add its own tip, and one person can even pay part cash and part card. Where to find it On a dine-in order (Table service), send the items to the kitchen, then tap Split among the buttons at the bottom right of the order screen ( Disc · Bill · Split · Pay Now ) — it is not inside the checkout screen you reach with Pay Now. Splitting is for table orders, so the button appears once the table's items have been sent. Split evenly (N빵) Buttons at the bottom right of the order screen ① Disc · ② Bill · ③ Split · ④ Pay Now Split the bill — Even split ① Total to split · ② Even split / By item · ③ Number of people − / + · ④ Start Split & Collect Tap Split , then choose Even split . Set the number of people with the − and + buttons. BrewDesk shows Each person pays underneath. Tap Start Split & Collect . Now collect one share at a time. The screen says "Person 1 of 4" . Take their cash or card, and it moves on to "Person 2 of 4" , and so on. After the last person, tap Start New Order — the table is paid off and cleared. Split by item (아이템별) Split the bill — By item ① By item · ② Tick the items · ③ Start Item Split Tap Split , then choose By item . Tick the items this person is paying for. BrewDesk adds them up. Tap Pay Selected and take their payment. Repeat with the next person's items until the "items left" count reaches zero. The order finishes on its own. Part cash, part card? On any share, switch the payment to Split Pay . Take the first part (say $5 cash) and BrewDesk shows Received and Remaining . Add a card for the rest — the share is done when Remaining reaches $0. Cash first, card last. On a Split Pay share, once any card has gone in, the Cash button goes grey and a note says "Cash first, card last. A card payment has already been taken for this round, so no more cash can be added." So take the cash part first, then finish with the card. This applies to a card you recorded by hand as well as one taken on a reader. Full single payments and settling an unpaid order are not affected. Show this off "엔빵" in three taps. Split evenly, split by item, or mix cash and card on the very same share — BrewDesk does the math and prints each person their own slip ("Split 1 of 4"). No calculator, no arguing at the table. Good to know: if you refund a share, the tip stays with the shop (only the item amount is returned), and BrewDesk won't let you close the day while a split is still half-paid.

t: Tips on orders you settle later
b: Tips on orders you settle later Sometimes an order is left unpaid and you settle it at the end of the day. If a tip is involved, BrewDesk now asks you about it before it takes the money — so a tip never quietly disappears. Where to find it At closing, tap an unpaid order and choose Settle unpaid order . The tip box is at the top of the payment screen. If the order already has a tip on it, you see "Tip recorded on this order" with two buttons — Include tip or Exclude tip . You must pick one; BrewDesk will not take the payment until you do. If there is no tip on the order but the customer tipped on your card terminal, use Add a tip . Type the amount and tap Apply . If you use staff accounts, pick who gets it under Tip goes to . This is required — a tip with no name on it can't reach anyone. Take the payment as normal. Tap Back to closing to carry on with the rest of your day. Why ask at all? Because a tip taken on a card terminal isn't in BrewDesk yet. If nobody types it in, your staff never see it. This one screen is where it gets in.

Cash payment rounding Cash Payment Rounding tidies up the odd coins. In a lot of countries the smallest coin is bigger than the last digit on the bill — nobody carries a 1-cent piece any more. So when a cash customer owes 10.03, you take 10.00 and let the 3 go. BrewDesk can now do that rounding for you, on cash payments only, and keep a record of every coin you let go. Where to find it Open Settings › Payments and scroll to Cash Payment Rounding . Only the store owner can open the Payments tab, so only the owner can set this. It starts off for every shop. Payments settings — payment methods & cash rounding ① Turn payment methods on/off · ② Enable cash payment rounding · ③ Rounding increment · ④ Save Turn on Enable cash payment rounding . Type the Rounding increment — the smallest coin you actually handle (0.05, 10, 100, whatever it is where you are). Leave it at 0 and the switch does nothing , which is exactly what the hint under the box tells you. Pick the Rounding direction : Nearest (up or down, whichever is closer), Round down (always in the customer's favour) or Round up . Look at the grey note underneath. BrewDesk knows the usual practice for your country and says so: "Common practice in this country: round to 0.05 using Nearest (legally required)." Tap Apply and it fills in the increment and direction for you. Tap Save at the top of Settings. Cash only — and your tax doesn't move. This only touches an order paid entirely in cash . Pay any part of it by card and the total stays exactly as it was. The tax amount is never recalculated, and card receipts print exactly as they did before. How the tax itself is rounded is a different setting, over in Settings › Tax & Service (see Set your tax ). "Legally required" vs "common practice". Some countries have a law about this (Singapore, Malaysia, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Switzerland among them); in others it's just what shops do. Either way BrewDesk only suggests — nothing changes until you tap Apply and Save. A few countries are listed as having no rounding practice at all ( "This country has no cash-rounding practice." ), and one we haven't checked yet says "This country has not been checked yet." The receipt shows the coins you let go. On any order where rounding actually changed the total, a Cash Rounding line prints just above the change line — on the paper receipt and the emailed one. Orders that landed on a round number don't get the line at all, so nothing looks cluttered. And it ties out at closing. Your closing report's Payment Breakdown gets a Cash Rounding line under Total Payment Collected, with the plain-words note "Coins not taken on cash payments. Payment Collected + this = Grand Total." That's the answer to "why is my drawer a few cents light?" — it isn't, you gave those coins away on purpose. You'll see the same figure on your payment history summary and on the Analytics cash card. Show this off Round like the shop next door, without losing the pennies in your books. Set the coin unit once and every cash total lands on a coin you actually have. Every rounded cent is still recorded, still on the receipt, and still adds up at closing — so your accountant never has to ask where the odd change went.

8 Discounts & promotions A discount takes money off a sale. You can set up happy hours and deals once, and BrewDesk does the math for you at the till. Discounts ① Add Discount · ② Totals cards (Active Promotions / Live Now / Automatic) · ③ A discount card · ④ ACTIVE on/off Create a discount ① Discount name · ② Type & value · ③ Schedule · ④ Where it applies Open Manage › Discounts in the left sidebar and tap Add Discount . The "Create Discount" form opens. Type a Discount Name . Pick the Discount Type — "Percentage" (like 10% off) or "Fixed Amount" (like $2 off) — and type the Value . Set the Schedule : a start and end date, "All Day" or a time range, "No End Date" if it never stops, and Repetition (does not repeat / weekly / monthly / custom). Choose where it applies under Applicable Scope : "All" items, or tick specific categories or items with the checkboxes. Logic & Applicability ① Item Level / Order Level · ② Automatic Application · ③ Manual Selection · ④ Minimum Order Value · ⑤ Allow Stacking Choose how it fires: Automatic (it comes off by itself at checkout) or Manual (staff tap "Apply Discount" at checkout and pick it). Optional: set a Minimum Order Value , and turn on Allow Stacking to let it combine with other discounts. Tap Save . Your discount is ready. Good to know: BrewDesk always works out the tax after the discount, so the total is always right.

Quick discount or free item Set-up discounts are for things that happen every week. This is for the one-off — a regular you want to look after, a drink you remade, a coffee for a friend. You do it right in the cart, in about three taps. Where to find it In the cart: tap an item, then Discount or Free on that line. For the whole order, tap the Disc button next to Bill at the bottom. Order-wide discount (Disc) keypad ① Custom amount, or a saved discount · ② $ Amount / % Percent · ③ Keypad · ④ Done Tap Discount on one item, or Disc for the whole order. A keypad panel opens. Choose how you want to type it — Amount (money off) or % Percent . Type the number on the keypad. Tap a reason chip — Friend , Apology , Staff , Tasting , Mistake — or "+ New" to write your own. Your own reasons come back next time. Tap Done . The cart total updates straight away. To take it off again, tap the same button — it now says Remove Discount (or Remove Free ). Order with a discount applied ① Disc button (applied count badge) · ② Discount line — Student Discount (10%) −$1.00 · ③ Total after discount Typed the full amount? BrewDesk asks "Full amount entered — record as Free instead?" and offers Record as Free . Say yes — then your reports can tell "given away" apart from "discounted", which is what you actually want to know at the end of the month. Made a discount in Settings and marked it "Manual"? It shows up as a tile inside this panel when you're adjusting the whole order, so staff just tap it instead of typing. If you haven't made any yet, there's a Create discount button that takes you to the right screen. Changed the quantity after discounting? The adjustment is cleared and you'll see "Adjustment cleared — quantity changed" . It's deliberate: 2,000 off two cups is not 2,000 off five cups, and BrewDesk would rather ask you again than quietly guess. Free items are shown on the closing summary on their own line — see Reports & closing the day .

9 Refunds A refund is when you give a customer their money back. BrewDesk makes this safe — a manager has to say yes first, so it can't be used the wrong way. Refunding from Payment History ① The order to refund · ② FAIR-REFUND button · ③ CHANGE PAYMENT METHOD button Refund a sale ① The items to refund · ② Refund Total (the amount to return) · ③ "REFUND FULL ORDER" button Go to Manage › Payment History in the left sidebar. Tap the order you want to refund to open it. Tap the FAIR-REFUND button under the receipt on the right (it is shown in capitals). Choose what to refund ① Tick the item(s) to refund · ② Refund Total · ③ REFUND FULL ORDER Choose full refund to give all the money back (works the same day). Or choose partial refund to give back only some items or some money. A manager types their PIN (a secret code) to say yes. Refund done ① REFUNDED filter · ② REFUNDED tag on the order card · ③ Red REFUNDED band on the receipt · ④ ORDER FULLY REFUNDED The refund is done. BrewDesk writes it down and fixes your day's totals for you. What is a PIN? It is a short secret code, like the one on a bank card. It stops a refund from happening by mistake. A partial refund now prints a partial receipt. The refund slip lists only the items you gave money back for — and the totals underneath (subtotal, discount, service charge, tax) are now the refunded share too , not the original order's figures. So the customer can add the slip up and it comes to exactly what went back on their card.

10 Reports & closing the day At the end of the day you check how the shop did and "close" the day. This locks in the day's numbers so they are safe. Here's how. Stats & daily insights ① Total Sales and the other total cards · ② Staff Sales and Attendance Log tabs (locked on the Starter plan) · ③ Revenue Trends chart Closing reports ① Close Now — start the day-close · ② Auto-Close toggle · ③ Accounting Export · ④ View a past Z-Report Close the day (Z-Report) ① Report type (X = interim, Z = final) · ② Grand total · ③ Operation summary · ④ Closed by — top row is role chips, bottom row is staff chips (staff chips appear when the Staff add-on is on) · ⑤ Close Day Closing Reports — by day ① Date range · ② Orders · Grand Total · ③ View (opens the Z-Report) · ④ Accounting Export Open Stats (it starts on Revenue Overview) to see your sales, how people paid, your best-selling items, and what each staff member sold. Read your AI daily insights ( Pro and above). This is a short note in plain words about your day, with helpful tips. ( Business plans also get one by email each week.) Count the cash in your drawer and check it matches the number BrewDesk shows. Add any money you put in, and note any money you took out. Z-Report ① Z-Report (Final) · ② Grand Total · ③ Total Transactions · ④ Payment Breakdown · ⑤ Print · Export · Close When the cash matches, go to Manage › Closing History (the screen is titled Closing Reports), tap Close Now , then tap Close Day in the window that opens. This saves a full summary of the day, called the Z-Report. What is closing the day? It just means you finish up for the day and save the totals. Doing it each night keeps your money records tidy. Practice orders are labelled, not hidden. Anything you rang up before going live now carries a Sandbox data badge in your payment history and your closing history — "Recorded during practice mode, before this store went live." Your Stats screen goes further and leaves them out of the numbers altogether, so your sales figures and staff sales are only real trading. If your totals look lower than they used to, this is why — they're right now. Had a partial refund today? The Z-Report shows a Refunds line in amber for any partial refunds. That amount is already counted in the Grand Total below it — the line is just there so the numbers tie out cleanly for you or your accountant. In the analytics report you download from Stats (CSV), "Net Profit" is now labeled Net Revenue (after tax) — a reminder it's revenue, not profit, since the cost of goods isn't subtracted. The Analytics Excel file in Backup & Restore may still use the older name. Gave something away today? The closing summary now shows a separate line under Discounts — "FREE ITEMS (3)" with Not deducted from total beneath it. Free is not the same as discounted: a discount is money you chose to give up on a sale, a freebie is stock that walked out with nothing coming back. Seeing them apart is how you notice when "just one on the house" becomes twenty a week. Rounding cash to the nearest coin? If you switched on cash payment rounding , the Payment Breakdown grows one line — Cash Rounding , right under Total Payment Collected, with "Coins not taken on cash payments. Payment Collected + this = Grand Total." underneath. That line is why collected and grand total differ, and it's the number to hand your accountant. If rounding is off, or nothing rounded today, the line doesn't appear at all. Cancelling an order asks why — always. Whether you void a leftover unpaid order at closing, void them all at once, or cancel an order out on the floor, the same little box appears: Wrong entry , Customer left , Test order , or Other (type a reason) . The confirm button stays greyed out until you pick one. Cancellations with no reason are exactly the ones you'll want an answer for later. Show this off Your numbers, said in plain words. Daily insights tell you what happened and what to do next — not just a page full of figures.

Export your sales Hand your numbers to your bookkeeper in one tap. Here's how. (The window is titled Backup & Restore — the same one described in Backups .) Accounting export — the window is titled "Backup & Restore" ① What to include · ② Ready-made QuickBooks / Xero formats · ③ Save to Drive (after connecting Google Drive) · ④ Download On the Closing Reports page (Manage › Closing History), tap Accounting Export . A window titled Backup & Restore opens. Tick what to include: Closing Report Summary , Daily Breakdown , All Transactions , or a ready-made QuickBooks Format / Xero Format . Tap Download to save the file, or Save to Drive to send it to your Google Drive. The format depends on what you ticked — Closing Report Summary and Daily Breakdown come as Excel (.xlsx); All Transactions, QuickBooks Format and Xero Format come as CSV. Save to Drive only works once Google Drive is connected. If the top of the window says "Google Drive not connected", tap Connect next to it (see Backups ). Download works either way. Easy bookkeeping: this makes your records simple — just hand the file to your accountant.

Late orders & missed days Two things sometimes happen around closing: a payment lands after you've already closed the day, or you simply forgot to close a day. BrewDesk handles both — and never changes your original Z-Report. A payment came in after closing — Additional Closing If you take a payment for a day that's already closed, BrewDesk warns you first: "This business day is already closed." The payment still goes through as normal. A little later a prompt appears: Additional Closing Needed . Tap Review & Close (or Not Now to handle it later). Check the late orders listed, then tap Confirm Additional Closing . BrewDesk saves a separate report called "Additional Closing #1" — your original Z-Report is never touched. Need the paper again? Open that day's closing report — each additional closing shows as a badge you can tap to reprint . (Additional closings print totals only, no payment-method or category breakdown.) You forgot to close a day Unclosed Business Days ① Notice that new orders and payments are blocked · ② The days still open · ③ Close One by One · ④ Auto-Close All The next time you open BrewDesk, an Unclosed Business Days window lists any day you missed. New orders and payments pause until those days are closed. Read "What should I do?" at the top. The easy choice is Auto-Close All — it closes every missed day at once using BrewDesk's expected totals (the cash count is skipped). Prefer to check each one? Tap Close One by One . If a day still has unpaid orders, tap Settle to pay or void them first. Paying off a bill that's already open still works. Only new business pauses. An order that's already sitting on a table can still be settled — Pay Now and Split stay available, so you can take the money, clear the order, and then close the day. The number it shows is the real one. If closing is refused because a bill is still unpaid, the message tells you how many orders the till is actually waiting on, so you know what to go and settle. Why block new sales? Closing days in order keeps your totals honest, so your reports — and your accountant's numbers — always line up.

Cash drawer You can balance the cash in your drawer for each shift. Put in the starting amount in the morning, note any money you add or take out, then count it at the end and see if it matches. Where to find it The Manage menu at the top → Cash Drawer . Only the owner and managers see this menu item. Opening the cash drawer from the Manage menu ① Manage icon in the sidebar · ② Cash Drawer Starting a cash drawer session ① SESSION / HISTORY tabs · ② Pay-In / Pay-Out buttons · ③ OPENING FLOAT (starting amount) · ④ Start Session When you open up, tap Start Session and enter the starting amount you put in the drawer. During the day, note money you add or remove as Pay In or Pay Out — bank drops, tip-outs, topping up change, and so on. At the end, tap "END SESSION" and enter what you actually counted. There are two ways: Enter Total types one total, or Count Denoms lets you enter how many of each note and coin and adds it up for you. BrewDesk shows Expected , Counted and Variance side by side. Cash sales are added in and money handed back as Cash Refunds is taken out. Then tap Close Day — the drawer figures go into that day's Z-Report with everything else. Not counting is recorded as "not counted," not as "zero difference." If you finish without entering anything, BrewDesk doesn't invent a variance of zero — it writes "Cash wasn't counted." Later, when you look back, "it balanced" and "nobody counted" won't look the same. Drawer not popping open by itself? The screen tells you why — ① no receipt printer is set up yet, ② the cash drawer setting is off on your main receipt printer (turn it on in Settings › Printers ), or ③ this device is a Sub POS. Either way, your figures are still recorded . If unpaid orders are still open , BrewDesk asks once more before it closes the drawer — "N unpaid order(s) still open for today. End the drawer session anyway?" That stops you closing the drawer while a bill is still waiting. Closing the drawer before the day is fine. Count it, tap END SESSION, then Close Day — what you counted and the variance still show up in the closing report and on the printout. An open drawer now holds the day open. If a drawer session is still running, the Close Day button is greyed out and a red line appears: "N cash drawer session(s) still open — count and end the drawer to close the day." Closing the day means the money is settled too, so BrewDesk won't let you sign off on a drawer nobody has counted. The way out is right there. Next to that message is an Open drawer button — tap it, count the cash, tap END SESSION , and the Close Day button comes back to life. You never have to hunt through menus to get unstuck. Someone went home without closing the drawer? The drawer screen shows "N cash drawer(s) were never closed" — "Someone left without ending the drawer. You cannot count it now, so closing it here records it as not counted — no number is invented." Tap Close without counting and you're free to carry on. The day is recorded honestly as "Cash wasn't counted" rather than as a tidy zero. Count first — the numbers come after. Until you type what you counted, BrewDesk hides the expected total (and the cash-sales and cash-refund lines that add up to it). In their place it says "Shown after you enter what you counted" and, underneath, "Count the drawer first, then the numbers appear. This is so the count stays a count." Your opening float and your pay-ins and pay-outs stay visible the whole time — you did those yourself, so there's nothing to hide. If the money doesn't match, one line is required. When the variance isn't zero, BrewDesk asks "Why is it different?" and won't let you close the drawer until something is written there (a blank space doesn't count). It nudges you with "Write one line before closing. In three days nobody will remember." — and it's right. If the variance is zero it doesn't ask at all. Who the drawer belongs to is picked, not typed. The old free-text name box is gone. If you use staff accounts, choose the person from the list under Drawer held by . If you don't use staff accounts, it simply says Owner — "Staff accounts are off, so this drawer is under the owner." The Recorded by box on a pay-in or pay-out is now read-only and follows the same person, so "who took that money out" only ever has one answer. Money leaving the drawer for supplies? There's now a Business expense reason on Pay-Out, alongside Safe Drop, Tip Out, Bank Drop and Other. Give it its own reason and at the end of the month you can actually add up where the cash went. Typed the opening float wrong? A Fix opening float button appears while nothing has happened yet — no cash sale, no pay-in, no pay-out. After the first cash sale it disappears, because by then changing the starting number would quietly move a real difference somewhere else. From that point on, write it in the variance reason at closing instead. The correction is added as a note (who, when, the old figure) — it never overwrites the original. A red band you can't dismiss. If a drawer change doesn't reach the server, you'll see "This drawer has not been saved" — "The last change did not reach the server. If you refresh now, the float, pay-ins and count are gone. Check the network and make any change again." There is no close button on purpose. A message you can swipe away is a message you'll forget, and refreshing the page would lose the day's drawer.

11 Working offline You don't always need the internet. If it stops, BrewDesk keeps working and saves everything. When the internet comes back, it catches up on its own. There is nothing for you to do. Working offline ① The orange bar means you're offline — keep taking orders; they save on the device and sync when you're back online If the internet drops, just keep taking orders the same as always. Your orders are saved right on the device, so nothing is lost. You can still print receipts while offline. When the internet comes back, everything sends up on its own. (That means it copies your orders to the cloud and tidies up.) Nothing gets sent twice. Show this off Always open for business. A weak signal or an outage won't stop even one sale. Many other tills only work with the internet on — BrewDesk doesn't have that problem.

Signing in offline Signing in while offline. With no internet, only an account that has already signed in on this device can get in. For any other account you'll see "You're offline. Only an account that has signed in on this device before can be used offline."

Pairing devices offline You can still add devices with no internet. Open the sign-in screen in the installed BrewDesk app while offline and you'll see "Can't reach the internet — looking for your store's main POS," then it moves to the find the main till screen on its own. As long as your shop Wi-Fi is up, you can pair a new tablet without any internet (see Add a device to your main till ). Your extra devices keep working too — over the shop Wi-Fi. When the internet drops, tablets and extra tills don't go quiet: they talk to your main till across your own shop network. Staff Ordering tablets still send orders, tables can still be seated, moved and merged, and the waitlist keeps running. All you need is the main till switched on and everyone on the same Wi-Fi. (If a tablet can't reach the main till, see the Not sent to the kitchen pop-up in 13.1.)

What needs the internet What still needs the internet. Three things wait for the connection to come back: sending texts (the waitlist Notify message and booking confirmations), making or editing a reservation (so two people can't book the same slot from outside the shop), and card payments . Everything else carries on. Lists don't go blank. If a page can't load, BrewDesk shows the last copy it received rather than an empty screen — you'll see "Showing the last list received" at the top. It refreshes on its own when you're back online.
12 Add-ons & extras Add-ons are extra features you can switch on or off. They all live in one place. You only pay for the ones you use.

Turn add-ons on and off Add-on store ① An on/off toggle (green = on) · ② Free / Pro+ label · ③ How many are on (number on / 16, next to Add-ons in the settings sidebar) Add-ons list ① On/off switch · ② Settings · ③ Upgrade (Pro+ add-ons) Open Settings › Add-ons . You'll see cards grouped as Operations , Guest Experience , and Devices , each with an on/off switch (green means on). Tap a switch to turn a feature on or off. Free add-ons work on every plan; some (like Online Ordering/QR, Loyalty, Staff, and Scheduler) are Pro ; SMS is pay-as-you-go. Some add-ons need another one first. Example: turning on Reservations while Tables is off shows a pop-up "Reservations requires Tables" — tap Enable Both . Turning off something other add-ons need shows Disable All . Next to Add-ons in the settings sidebar there's a small counter ("number on / 16") showing how many of the 16 add-ons are on. For text messages (SMS), add some money to your balance first (see Messaging your customers ). Then you only pay for the texts you actually send. Pay-as-you-go means you pay a little as you use it, instead of a set monthly price. Top up when your balance runs low.

When a feature is locked Staff tapped something that's locked? They can ask you, from there. On the web, tapping a locked feature (Staff Ordering, Customer Display, Waitlist Kiosk) offers to send you the instructions instead of leaving them stuck: "Want us to email the owner instructions for turning on Staff Ordering?" → Send email . You get it in your inbox, they get on with the queue. It only sends once a day per feature — a second try says "We already sent that email today — please check your inbox." On an iPad or the desktop app you get a short explanation instead of the email button (App Store rules) — change your plan from your BrewDesk account on the web.

13 Your plan & billing A plan is the level of BrewDesk you use. You can start for free and move up later. You manage it all in one place. Plans & billing ① Billing & invoices · ② Free trial — days left & Add payment · ③ Your current plan · ④ Upgrade You can stay on the Starter plan, which is free. Or you can try Pro or Business free for one month. You don't need a credit card to start the trial. When you decide to keep going, add a way to pay (like a card). To check your plan, your payment card, or your bills, go to Billing . The price is set to suit the country you are in. A free trial means you use the full plan for a month at no cost. If you don't want to keep it, you simply don't add a card. Check your store from your phone: sign in to the owner app ( brewdesk.io/owner ) — its guide opens from the Manual button at the top of the owner app.

Deleting your account Closing the shop, or moving on from BrewDesk? You can delete your account. Nothing disappears the moment you tap it — it runs 14 days later , and you can undo it any time before that. Where to find it Open your account settings from the account menu at the top right, then the Delete Account tab. Only the owner can do this. The menu from the profile icon (D) at the bottom left ① Profile & Account · ② Check for updates Delete Account tab (just look — do not run it) ① Delete Account tab · ② TYPE DELETE TO CONFIRM — type DELETE · ③ YOUR CURRENT PASSWORD Read the list of what goes — store details, menu, order and payment history, subscription and invoices, closing reports, all of it. If you might need any of it later, tap Export data and save a copy first. Once it runs, there's no way to get it back. Type DELETE in capital letters in the confirm box. Tap Send verification code . A 6-digit code goes to the owner's email. Enter the code from the email. The button then shows the real date (for example "Delete account on August 14, 2026" ) — tap it, and you're booked in and signed out. Changed your mind? Sign back in and you'll see a banner across the top plus a Deletion D-N badge counting down. Just tap Cancel deletion and it's off — no code needed this time. The owner and managers can cancel it. Your shop keeps running for those 14 days. Orders and payments work exactly as normal. Subscription billing is paused, and you can't switch plans while the countdown is on. Why the email code? So nobody can wipe out your shop by accident — or on purpose. Only someone who can open the owner's inbox can schedule it. Good to know: we keep a separate record of deletion requests and cancellations, so if there's ever an "I didn't delete that" moment, it can be checked.

Change your login email If you mistyped your email when you signed up, the verification mail is going somewhere you can't reach — and resending it just sends it to the same wrong place again. Now you can correct the address yourself. Where to find it Account menu (top right) → Account Settings → Profile tab → "Wrong email address? Change it" . Owner account only. Account Settings — Profile tab ① Delete Account tab · ② Wrong email address? Change it Change email form (just look — do not run it) ① NEW EMAIL ADDRESS · ② CURRENT PASSWORD · ③ Change email & send link Tap "Wrong email address? Change it" . The form shows your current address so you can see what's wrong. Type the New email address — the one you can actually receive mail at. Type your Current password . This is required: your email is also how you sign in, so BrewDesk checks it's really you. Tap Change email & send link . You'll see "Saved. A verification link is on its way to … — open it to unlock BrewDesk." Open your mail and tap the link. Done. Nothing locks you out at day seven any more. The old "verify or you're locked" popup is gone. Instead there's a quiet banner with a Resend button — and now, next to it, a way to fix the address itself. Resending to a typo was never going to work. If the address is already taken by another BrewDesk account, you'll be told plainly rather than left wondering. Same for a wrong password.

Installer partner Some shops are set up by a local installer or dealer, who keeps a hand on the menu and the settings for you. If that's you, you can see exactly who has that access — and end it yourself, whenever you like. Where to find it Account menu (top right) → Installer partner . Owner account only , and the menu item only appears when there is an approved connection — no menu for shops that don't use an installer, or that only have a request waiting. Open it. You'll see who is connected and since when — "Connected since 3 Feb 2026" — and if another installer has asked and is still waiting, "Awaiting your approval" with the date they asked is shown too. To end it, tap Disconnect next to their name. Confirm: "This installer will lose access to this store immediately. You can approve them again later if you change your mind." The decision is yours, not theirs. Only the store owner can disconnect an installer — an installer can't quietly remove the record of their own access. A request that is still waiting is handled in the approval email the installer's request sends to the owner, not in this menu — that email has both an approve and a decline link. While an installer is working in your shop on your behalf, their name is shown on their screen and recorded next to what they did in your activity log — so "who changed this price?" always has an answer.

14 Staff & permissions Here you add the people who work for you. You can pick what each one is allowed to do, and track their work hours. (This needs the Pro or Business plan.) Where to turn it on Turn it on in Settings › Add-ons › Staff (a Pro add-on; only the owner can turn it on). Staff ① Add staff · ② Idle Lock on/off (was "PIN Login") · ③ Staff list Go to Settings and find the staff page. Tap Add staff . Type the person's name. Give them a role. The role decides what they can and can't do in the app. Turn on Idle Lock if you want the till to lock itself when nobody's using it. (This used to be called "PIN Login".) Turn on the time clock so staff can tap to start and end their shift. Their hours go into your reports for you. You can put a staff member's name on an order any time — even after the sale is done. (This is handy for salons.) A role is the set of things a person is allowed to do. For example, only a manager might be allowed to give refunds.

Staff add-on on vs off Staff features are fully on only when both are true: (1) your plan is Pro or Business , and (2) the Staff toggle in Settings › Add-ons is on . If either is missing, parts are locked as shown below. Add-on ON ① Staff toggle on · ② Settings next to it opens staff settings Add-on OFF ① Staff toggle off · ② The Settings button next to it disappears Starter plan ① Lock icon · ② "Staff management is Pro-only" · ③ Upgrade Pro Stats, add-on ON ① Staff Sales · ② Attendance Log tabs are open Stats, add-on OFF ① Staff Sales · ② Attendance Log tabs are locked Lock screen ① Select Profile screen · ② Pick a name, then enter the PIN ON : the Staff Sales and Attendance Log tabs in Stats open (the Stats screen starts on Revenue Overview). Payment History gets an All Staff filter and the Close Day window shows staff chips. With Idle Lock also on, the register shows a Select Profile lock screen so each person switches to their own profile. OFF : those tabs show a lock, and the All Staff filter, Close Day staff chips and lock screen do not appear. Adding and viewing people in Settings › Staff Permissions › Staff still works on Pro, whatever the toggle. Starter plan : the Add-ons card shows an Upgrade button instead of a toggle. The Staff sub-tab shows only a lock, "Staff management is Pro-only" and an Upgrade Pro button. Relation to the Scheduler: Scheduler Staff Columns depend on the Pro plan plus having staff accounts , not on this toggle (see Reservations & Scheduler ). Starter has no Scheduler tab at all.

Add a staff member Add a staff member ① Name · ② Role (Manager / Cashier) · ③ PIN (4 digits) + confirm · ④ Add staff Right after saving ① "added as staff" notice · ② the new person in the list Staff list (after adding) ① Add staff · ② Idle Lock · ③ staff list (role badge, status) Tap Add staff . A form opens. Type the person's Name . Pick a Role — Manager (menu, orders, reports — no billing or staff changes) or Cashier (take orders, see today's sales). Set a 4-digit PIN and confirm it. Tap Add staff . They now appear in your staff list and can sign in with their PIN.

Edit or remove a person Fixing a name, changing a PIN, hiding someone who left — these used to be four different little controls on the same row. Now there is one door: tap the person. Edit staff card (opens when you tap the staff name) ① Name · ② Role · ③ PIN (leave both blank to keep) · Reset · Revoke · ④ Save In your staff list, tap the staff name (anywhere on that person's row) . The edit window opens. Their email is at the top so you can be sure it's the right person. Fix the Name if you need to. Change the Role if their job changed. (An owner's row shows the role as plain text — an owner's role can't be changed here.) To set a new PIN, type it in both PIN (4 digits) boxes. Leave both boxes blank and the current PIN stays as it is — the screen says so, right under the boxes. Tap Save . That's it. Half-typed PINs don't slip through. If you type even one digit, BrewDesk asks for all four and asks you to type it twice. A PIN that's quietly ignored is worse than no PIN. Hide someone instead of deleting them. Disable takes them off the POS but keeps their past orders and hours in your reports. Enable brings them back. Only the owner sees these buttons. Invited the wrong person as an owner? You can now remove an owner too — before, there was no way to undo that. Two things still can't happen, and BrewDesk tells you which: you can't remove yourself , and you can't remove the last owner of the shop. Removing anyone asks you to confirm the name, then asks for the owner PIN ("Owner PIN required to remove staff member."). Removing someone is not the same as handing the shop over. If you're selling the business, ask us about transferring ownership instead.

Permissions, manager PIN & role chip This settings page shows, screen by screen, what a manager and a cashier are each allowed to do — and now you can actually tick the boxes and save . The whole page was rebuilt: your two PIN cards sit side by side across the top, with the big table below. Where to find it Settings › Staff Permissions . Managers can open it and read it; only the owner can change and save it . Two tabs sit at the top — Permissions (everyone gets this) and Staff (a Pro feature: "Staff management is Pro-only"). Staff Permissions ① Owner PIN — Set PIN · ② Manager PIN — Change PIN · ③ Permissions / Staff tabs · ④ Manager and Staff columns — ticks and padlocks (PIN approval) Permissions table (open from the start) ① screen row (Manager and Staff columns) · ② permission rows underneath · ③ PIN approval marker The table has exactly two columns — "Manager" and "Staff" . There's no owner column, because the owner always has every permission. The table is open from the start — there is nothing to fold or unfold. Permissions are grouped by screen ( Screens · Settings tabs · Available everywhere ), with the detailed permission rows right under each screen. A screen with no detailed permissions is just a single row. Tick or untick a box for that role. The box on a screen row decides whether that role can open the screen ; the boxes underneath decide the individual actions. A row you've changed from its default shows a reset marker. Watch the coloured pills next to some rows: PIN approval (a manager has to type a PIN first), Limited view (they see part of it), Restricted (blocked), and Open the page — the one that decides whether the screen appears at all. A row with a padlock can't be changed, even by the owner (owner-only or fixed items). The table has no search box or "Differences only" switch, so scan it from top to bottom. Tap Save at the top of Settings when you're done. Unsaved rows are counted for you, and Discard changes puts everything back. Every row you see in the table is really enforced. Untick a box and that role is actually stopped, with a popup saying so. The table currently has refunds , managing discounts , recalculating a closing & settling tips , adding staff & resetting their PINs and saving settings , and opening a screen at all ( Open the page ) is enforced too — see the next two tips. Managers can no longer save settings by default. This one changed: "saving settings" now starts off for managers. A manager can still open a settings screen and read it, but tapping Save brings up "You don't have permission for this" — "Only the store owner can make this change. You can still view this screen." If your manager used to save settings for you, tick that box here to give it back. You can hand a manager whole settings tabs. Eleven settings tabs can be opened up to a manager — Hours & Closures , Receipts , Printers , Devices , Staff Permissions (read-only), Activity Log , Support , Tables , Waitlist , Reservations and Staff . Fourteen stay owner-only no matter what, because they're the money and the identity of the shop: Store Info, Tax & Service, Payments, Notifications, Add-ons, Tips, Order Types, Customers, Customer Portal, Scheduler, Display & Branding, Loyalty, Google Drive and Messaging. Those don't have a box to tick. When someone hits a screen you switched off they get told plainly, in place of the screen: "The store owner turned this screen off for your role" — "Access to this screen was switched off for your role under Settings › Staff Permissions. Signing in again won't restore it — ask the store owner to turn it back on." That last sentence matters: this is a setting, not a glitch, so logging out and back in won't help them. Every save emails you. Whenever permissions are saved, the store owner gets an email saying what changed — so nobody can quietly widen their own access. The same change only emails once a day. Idle Lock off doesn't switch any of this off. Turning Idle Lock off (under Settings › Staff Permissions › Staff ) only stops the till locking itself — nothing more. Staff still sign in with their own PIN, the role chip still switches, the activity log still records who did what, and every permission on this page is still enforced. (Turning the Staff add-on off is the switch that stops people being told apart.) The PIN cards — side by side across the top of this page The owner PIN and manager PIN cards live on this same page, side by side across the top. Each one tells you its state at a glance: Set , "Default 0000" or Not set . Under the owner card: "Locks after 10 min idle" once it's set, or "Set it to enable the lock screen" if it isn't. The manager PIN lets whoever is on shift do manager things without a separate account for them — only the owner can set or change it. A manager opening this page sees a padlock and "Only the owner can change this card." Still on 0000? Then Manager is shut. The card says so — status chip "Default 0000" and, underneath, "Can't switch to Manager until you change it" . While the manager PIN is the factory 0000, nobody can switch this till to Manager at all : typing 0000 gets "This PIN is still the default, so it can't be used to switch roles. Set a new PIN first." Change it once and Manager works. (This is on purpose — a shop-wide code everyone already knows isn't a lock.) Worth knowing before you rely on it: your activity log will say Manager , not who . If you need to know which person did something, give people their own staff accounts ( Pro ). The role chip — switching who this till is right now Role chip panel ① role chip (Owner) · ② Owner · Manager · Staff row · ③ Staff Settings Look at the top bar: there's a coloured chip showing what this POS is acting as — Owner (amber), Manager (blue) or Staff (grey). Tap it. A small panel opens with the three roles listed. Stepping down (owner → staff, say, when you hand the till to someone) is one tap. No PIN — you're giving power away, not taking it. Stepping up asks for that role's PIN ("Enter the manager PIN"). Rows this device isn't allowed to reach are greyed out before you tap, so you never hit a dead end. BrewDesk won't let you lock yourself out on the way down. If there's no working PIN to climb back up with, stepping down is refused before it happens: "Set the owner PIN first. Without it, this device could not switch back up after stepping down." Set your owner PIN and it's one tap again. (A PIN still sitting on the factory 0000 doesn't count as a way back.) Typed the PIN wrong five times? That one device pauses PIN switching for 15 minutes : "Too many PIN attempts on this device — it's locked for a few minutes. Other devices and personal PIN sign-in are not affected." Read that last part — your other tills carry on, and anyone with their own staff PIN can still sign in normally, so the queue keeps moving. The owner also gets an email about repeated wrong tries, at most one a day.

Forgot a PIN? Nobody has to phone support because a PIN went out of somebody's head. Each PIN has its own way back. The owner PIN — a code to your email Where to find it Tap the role chip in the top bar (the same panel you use to switch role). On the owner row there's "Forgot your PIN?" . You must be signed in as the owner on this device. Tap "Forgot your PIN?" . BrewDesk emails a 6-digit code to the account email: "We sent a 6-digit code to your account email. Enter it below along with a new PIN." Type the Email code , then your New PIN (4 digits) , and confirm it. Tap Set new PIN . You'll see "Owner PIN reset. Use the new PIN next time." The code doesn't hang around. It expires after 10 minutes , and 5 wrong tries lock it — you'll see "Too many incorrect attempts. Request a new code." Just send yourself a fresh one. Too simple a PIN is refused too: "That PIN is too simple — choose a different 4 digits." You get an email even when it was you. Every owner PIN reset sends a confirmation to the owner's inbox. If one ever arrives and it wasn't you, that's your early warning. The manager PIN — the owner just sets a new one Change manager PIN (open only) ① NEW PIN (4 DIGITS) · ② CONFIRM PIN · ③ Change PIN Open Settings › Staff Permissions and find the manager PIN card across the top. Tap Change PIN (or Set PIN if there isn't one yet) and type the new code. Owner only. Tell the counter the new code. The "Reset to 0000" button is gone from the manager PIN.
