It used to be there; it isn't any more, and there's nothing to miss — resetting to 0000 only ever left the shop with a code everybody knew, and 0000 can't be used anyway. Just set the new PIN directly. One staff member's PIN is different: Settings › Staff Permissions › Staff , open that person, and "Reset to 0000" is still there for you — an owner or a manager can use it. Have them set their own PIN straight away afterwards. 0000 doesn't work anywhere. Signing in with the default gets "The default PIN (0000) can't be used to sign in. Ask the owner to set a new PIN in Settings, or use ‘Forgot your PIN?’ there." — and now switching role with it is refused too: "This PIN is still the default, so it can't be used to switch roles. Set a new PIN first." A forgotten reset can't quietly become an open door.

15 Reservations & Scheduler A reservation is when a customer books a table or a time before they come in. You can keep all your bookings in one place. Let's add one. Where to turn it on Turn Reservations on in Settings › Add-ons › Reservations (flip the switch). It needs Tables on first — if Tables is off, a pop-up offers "Enable Both," just tap it. Salon and spa bookings (by staff member and time) use the Scheduler add-on in the same place — it is a Pro add-on. Before you begin: set your opening hours in Settings › Hours & Closures . Reservations only offer times that fall inside your open shifts — so if a time isn't showing, check your hours first. Scheduler: staff columns ① One column per staff member Scheduler: no staff ① Hint to add staff first Reservation settings ① Settings / Special Days tabs · ② Booking rules (slot, party size, window) · ③ Save New reservation ① Walk-in / Reservation · ② Guest name & phone · ③ Date & time (Duration and Chair / Room follow below) · ④ Save Reservation. This is the salon/spa layout; restaurants see a Table box and a Guests box instead of Chair / Room. Open the reservations page. From the Table Map , tap Reservations (top right) — or open the Scheduler tab at the top. (The Scheduler tab only shows on the Pro plan with the Scheduler add-on turned on.) Tap the day you want on the calendar. Tap New Reservation . A form opens. New Reservation form ① Walk-in / Reservation · ② Guest Name (required) · ③ Phone (required) · ④ Date · Time · ⑤ Save Reservation Fill in the Guest Name , Phone (both required), Date , and Time . Email is optional, and Duration starts at 1 hour. In table shops such as restaurants and cafes you also pick the number of Guests (1–4, or type 5 and up). Salon and spa style shops have no guest-count box. Optional: pick a Table (or a Chair / Room in salons and spas) and a Staff member, and add a Note . For a salon or spa, picking the staff member is the main thing. The Staff box only appears once at least one staff member has been added. Tap Save . The guest automatically gets a confirmation that says "you're booked" — by email, SMS, or WhatsApp, depending on what you've set up. Reservation list ① Reservations button · ② Upcoming / Seated / Past · ③ Reservation card — tap to open · ④ New Reservation When a booked guest arrives, open their reservation card and tap Check In . It turns to Seated (and gives them a table if needed). Someone walks in with no booking? Tap the Walk-in option — it seats the guest right away. Seated bookings close themselves. Once a reservation is Seated , it moves into past bookings on its own when that table gets paid , when the order is cancelled , or when you close out the day . No more yesterday's guests sitting in your reservation list. Guests who never turned up — mark them all at closing. Switch on Auto No-Show on Close in Settings › Reservations › Settings , under Booking Policy & Guest Portal . Then, as the description says: "closing the day automatically marks any still-Confirmed reservations from that day as No-Show, and sends each guest a notice email explaining why." It's off until you turn it on. Only bookings still sitting at Confirmed are touched — seated, completed and cancelled ones are left exactly as they are, and re-closing the same day won't email anyone twice. The guest's email is matter-of-fact, not a telling-off: the subject is "We couldn't confirm your visit" , it says the table was held but the arrival couldn't be confirmed, and it invites them to contact you if that's wrong. Scheduler vs Reservations: the Scheduler ( Pro , Scheduler add-on) is for salon/spa appointments (booked by staff member and time). Table reservations are for dining (a party at a table). They share the same calendar area, so all your bookings live in one place. Scheduler Staff Columns: per-staff columns appear in the Scheduler only on the Pro plan and when you have staff accounts . This is separate from the Staff add-on toggle (see Staff & permissions ). With no staff yet, a hint message is shown. Starter has no Scheduler tab. No internet? Check-ins still work. With the internet down you can still tap Check In , No Show or Cancel — the change shows on screen straight away and uploads by itself when you're back online. Only making or editing a booking is blocked, and the screen tells you why: "Cannot create a reservation while offline — the booking calendar is also written from outside the store, so it could double-book. Reconnect and try again." If the list can't load at all you'll see "Showing the last list received," and the bookings you already had stay on screen. Show this off Bookings come built in. You don't need a second app or an extra fee. Restaurants book tables; salons and spas book staff time — all on the same calendar.

Waitlist A waitlist is the line of guests waiting for a free table. BrewDesk holds the line for you, and texts a guest the moment their table is ready — so they don't have to crowd your door. Where to turn it on Turn it on in Settings › Add-ons › Waitlist (flip the switch). It needs Tables on first — tap Enable Both if a pop-up asks. Add to waitlist ① Guest name · ② Party size · ③ Phone (so they can be texted) · ④ "Add to Waitlist" Open the Waitlist . From the Table Map , tap Waitlist (top right). Tap Add Guest . A small form opens. Enter the guest's Name , Party size (how many people), and Phone (so they can be texted). Add a note if you like, then save. When a table frees up, find that guest and tap Notify . They get a "your table is ready" text (SMS or WhatsApp). Then seat them — and you're done. Why add a phone number? The phone number is how the guest gets the "table ready" text. Without it, you'd have to call their name the old-fashioned way. The line keeps moving with no internet. Adding a guest, seating, No Show and Cancel all work offline. You'll see "Saved on this device" and it uploads on its own when the connection returns — a guest added offline gets their ticket number after it uploads . Refreshing the screen won't lose the line either: it's kept on the device, and you'll see "Showing the last list received." The one thing that needs internet is Notify — the "your table is ready" text can't go out until you're back online, so call that guest by name for now. No tables? Call the guest and start their order. If your shop runs as a counter (no table map), the button on the guest's card says Start Order instead of Seat . Tap it and BrewDesk marks them seated and drops you straight into the order screen for that guest. If something is already in the basket it asks first — Order in progress → tap Hold & start and the old basket is parked in your held orders, so nothing is lost. Your kiosk wears your name. On a tablet set to Waitlist Kiosk , the top of the screen now shows your shop logo and shop name — it uses the picture you already saved in Settings › Store info , so there is nothing extra to upload. The phone box also opens on your country's dialling code (+1, +82, +66 …), taken from your shop's country, so guests just type their number.

16 Customers & loyalty This part helps your customers come back. BrewDesk builds a list of your customers all by itself, and you can reward people for visiting again. Where to turn it on Turn on loyalty stamps in Settings › Add-ons › Loyalty / Stamps (a Pro add-on); it needs CRM/Customers on first (tap Enable Both if asked). For the line-up, turn on Settings › Add-ons › Waitlist (needs Tables on first). Customers ① Add Customer · ② Search · ③ Totals (total / active / new) · ④ A customer row Link a customer to the order ① Link Customer · ② Search by name or phone · ③ Tap a result Just take orders as normal. BrewDesk quietly builds a customer list from those orders. Customer details ① Tap a customer in the list · ② Name and contact · ③ Visits · Spent · Avg Order · Reservations · ④ Consent · ⑤ Edit Customer Tap a customer's name any time to see how often they have visited. Want to reward regulars? Turn on loyalty stamps . This gives each customer a digital stamp card (like a coffee card on their phone). Customers earn a stamp each visit. After enough stamps, they get a reward, like a free drink. Got a queue? Use the waitlist to hold the line, then send a text when a table is ready. Show this off Your customer list grows on its own. No paper, no typing names in. Every order quietly adds to your regulars list and their visit history.

Loyalty stamps How to set it up and earn. A stamp card on the phone. Each visit earns a stamp; enough stamps win a reward. Here's how to set it up and use it. Loyalty settings ① Overview / Settings tabs · ② Set how many stamps are required (Stamps Required) · ③ Save Set it up. Open Settings › Add-ons , turn the Loyalty / Stamps card ON , then tap the card's Settings button. The Loyalty screen opens with two tabs: Overview and Settings . Set the stamp count and reward in the Settings tab. Choose how many stamps earn a reward ( Stamps Required , like 10). Pick the reward — a Free Item or a "% Discount" — and give it a name. Choose how long the reward lasts, then tap Save . How a customer earns a stamp: when you take their order, tap Link Customer and pick them (or add them). When the order is paid, they get a stamp. Redeem a reward: once they have enough stamps, a reward shows on their next order — tap Use Reward to take it off the bill. Turn it on first: loyalty needs the CRM/Customers add-on on first (this is noted in the box above — tap Enable Both if asked).

17 QR code ordering A QR code is that little square pattern people scan with their phone camera. With it, customers can order and pay from their own phone. They don't have to download anything. QR ordering is order-only — guests browse the menu, add to a cart, and pay. Where to turn it on Turn it on in Settings › Add-ons › Online Ordering (this is QR ordering, a Pro add-on). Flip the switch on. Add-ons — Online Ordering card ① Online Ordering switch (on) · ② Settings button on the card Table QR ordering settings ① Table QR Ordering tab · ② Fixed table QR switch · ③ Print all fixed QRs · ④ Show / Print QR for each table Table QR code (to print) ① Table number and QR code ("Scan to order") · ② Print The customer's phone (after scanning) ① Store name and table number · ② Category tabs · ③ Menu card — tap to add Go to the Add-on store in Settings and turn on QR ordering . (This needs the Pro or Business plan.) BrewDesk makes a QR code for each table. Tap to print them. Put one QR code on each table. A customer points their phone camera at the code. Your menu opens on their phone — no app to download. They browse the menu, add what they want to a cart, and pay. The order then pops up on your till by itself. No app needed. The customer just uses their normal phone camera. There is nothing for them to install. One thing to know: the QR ordering page is for ordering and paying only . Booking a table (reservations) and joining the line (waitlist) are not part of the QR page — your staff handle those in the POS (see Reservations & Scheduler ). This keeps things simple for the guest.

Running it day to day QR orders need your main till on. QR (and online) orders come in through your main till. If your main till is off or offline, new QR orders pause for a moment and the guest sees a short "please try again in a moment" note — the order goes through as soon as your main till is back. Making a table's QR after hours? If you print a table's QR code by hand outside your opening times, BrewDesk asks you to confirm first, so a code never goes out by mistake. Automatic and bulk seating aren't affected. Don't print new table QRs while the internet is down. If your till can't reach BrewDesk and you try to issue a QR, it stops you first: "Check the internet connection — can't issue a table QR." A guest who scanned that code would order into thin air — the order wouldn't arrive at your till. Take orders yourself until the connection is back.

What guests see What the guest sees: on their phone, a guest can open My Orders to see today's and earlier orders, with an item-by-item bill. After they pay, they need to scan the QR again to start a fresh order — this stops a paid order from being added to by accident. Gallery or list view. Guests can switch the phone menu between a gallery view (big food photos) and a simple list. Items without a photo show your store logo instead, so the menu always looks tidy. Whichever view a guest picks is remembered on their phone.

18 Messaging your customers You can send your customers a receipt or a quick note. You can pick the way they like best — email, WhatsApp, or text. Where to turn it on Manage all three channels — email, SMS and WhatsApp — in Settings › Messaging . WhatsApp is not an add-on; it is a channel on this screen. SMS and WhatsApp are pay-as-you-go — add a little credit and you only pay for what you send.

t: Turn on a channel & top up
b: Turn on a channel & top up On the Usage tab of Messaging you'll see three cards side by side: Email , SMS (Credit Balance) and WhatsApp (WA Credit). Each card shows the credit left, how many you sent this month, a Top Up button and an Auto Top-Up switch. Email is ready to go from day one. Use it to send receipts and daily reports. WhatsApp doesn't need the add-on store. Turn the channel on in the WhatsApp card and add some credit, and you can send receipts, rewards, and "your table is ready" notes. When you turn the channel on you get an email to finish setting it up, and until you top up the card says "Enabled · add credit to send". A plain text message (an SMS ) works the same way. Top up on the SMS card and you only pay for the texts you send. When credit runs low, tap Top Up at the top of that card. If you'd rather not keep topping up, turn on Auto Top-Up at the bottom of the card and choose how low it can get before it adds more, and how much to add. (In the iPad and desktop apps the card shows a channel on/off switch instead of a payment link.)

Opt-in & templates Customers always say yes first before you message them. If they ever reply STOP, BrewDesk stops texting them right away. You'll find the wording of each message in the Templates tab and what was sent in the Log tab. Opt-in means the customer chooses to get your messages. They are always in control. Messaging ① Usage / Templates / Log tabs · ② Credit left on each card · ③ Top Up · ④ Auto Top-Up

19 Backups A backup is a spare copy of all your shop's information. BrewDesk can save one to your own Google Drive, so your data is always safe. Backup ① Connected to Google Drive · ② Back Up Now · ③ Backup History Go to Settings and find the backup page. Tap Connect Google Drive and sign in to your Google account. That's it. From now on, BrewDesk saves a fresh backup on its own, again and again. Backup history ① Type (SNAPSHOT) · ② Status (success) · ③ Restore (check carefully before tapping) Ever need an old copy back? Tap Restore and pick a backup. Google Drive is a free online place to keep files. The backup goes into your own Drive, so only you can see it.

20 Equipment & network Everything to prepare before installing BrewDesk in a store — devices, printers, card readers and the network — in one place. It gathers tips spread across the device modes , device pairing , offline and printer chapters, in installation order. For the actual install sequence, follow Installation checklist .

Devices You can use tablets and computers you already own. However, connecting devices to each other (registering staff ordering, customer display and waitlist kiosk devices) only works in the installed BrewDesk app . Device How it's used · notes iPad Install the BrewDesk app . It can take any job: main till, extra till, staff ordering, customer display or waitlist kiosk. It prints straight from the app to Wi-Fi/LAN printers or AirPrint printers ( Receipts & printers ). Android tablet Not supported yet (the Android app is in preparation). Use an iPad or the desktop app for now. Computer (Mac · Windows) The BrewDesk desktop app is recommended. USB printers are connected through the desktop app's Select installed printer , so a till with a USB printer needs the desktop app ( Receipts & printers ). Web browser You can sign up, set up and even run a till at brewdesk.io. But a browser screen can't be registered as a new device ("Add devices from the BrewDesk app"), and Wi-Fi printing from a browser may ask you to install a helper program (Print Bridge). Install the app on any device that stays in the store. How many devices? It depends on the plan — tills (including the main one): Starter and Pro 1 , Business 3 . Customer displays: Pro 1 , Business 3 . Staff ordering devices: Pro 3 , Business unlimited. Extra tills (Sub POS) are a Business feature ( Device modes & customer display , device limit ). Make the main till a device that stays on all day. Orders from staff-ordering tablets and QR / online orders all pass through the main till. If it goes off, QR / online ordering pauses, and nothing switches to another device automatically. To connect other devices, the main till must also be running the BrewDesk app ( Multiple devices & reliability ). Devices ① Main POS (this device) · ② Customer Display switch ( Pro and above) · ③ Disconnect · ④ Note: add devices from the BrewDesk app

Receipt & kitchen printers Printers ① Add Printer · ② A connected printer card (status, role, Test) · ③ Setup Guide · ④ Print Log Type — any standard thermal receipt printer . The defaults suit 80mm paper (42 characters per line). Wi-Fi / LAN printers — connect with the printer's IP address and port (usually 9100 ). If you don't know the IP, tap Search . Put the printer on the same router as the tills. USB printers — install the printer driver on the computer as usual (Mac is usually automatic, Windows uses the maker's driver), then pick it from the list in the desktop app. Role — give each printer a role: Main Receipt (customer receipts) or Kitchen (kitchen tickets). One printer can do both, and selling works fine with no kitchen printer at all. Cash drawer — the drawer opens through the receipt printer, and its cash-drawer option must be on in the printer settings. The drawer does not open from an extra till (Sub POS) ( Cash drawer ). Check with a test print. Use Test Print to confirm paper actually comes out and text isn't cut off or garbled. Some Wi-Fi printers can't report whether they printed ( No print confirmation ), so check with your eyes ( Receipts & printers ).

Card readers Payments settings — payment methods & cash rounding ① Turn payment methods on/off · ② Enable cash payment rounding · ③ Rounding increment · ④ Save Connected card readers — BrewDesk uses Stripe Terminal readers. Money goes straight to the owner's own Stripe account. Readers are bought from the Stripe Dashboard. Connecting — first connect the owner's Stripe account in Settings › Payments . Power on the reader, put it on the same network as the till, then in the card reader section of the same screen tap Discover Readers → Connect . An existing separate terminal — stores that take cards on a terminal not connected to BrewDesk record them with the card-brand buttons on the payment screen ( Record Only ). Make sure Card (Record Only) is on in Settings › Payments ( Getting paid ). Connected card payments need the internet. When it drops you'll need another way to get paid, so we recommend leaving the Cash payment method on ( What needs the internet ).

Wi-Fi & network BrewDesk devices talk to the main till over the store's own network , even when the internet is down. That makes the router the most important part of the install. Everything on the same store Wi-Fi (same router) — the main till, extra tills, staff-ordering tablets, customer displays, network printers and card readers all go on one network. Different Wi-Fi networks are the most common reason devices can't find each other. No guest Wi-Fi, no phone hotspots — if the store runs a separate guest Wi-Fi, keep store devices on the store Wi-Fi only. A device on guest Wi-Fi is told "This device is outside the store network". Turn off AP isolation — if the router has "AP isolation" or "wireless isolation" switched on, devices can't talk to each other even on the same Wi-Fi. Turn it off for the store Wi-Fi. Give printers a static IP — if a Wi-Fi/LAN printer's IP address changes, BrewDesk keeps printing to the old one. Setting a static IP on the printer or router avoids that. Changed the router? — devices may no longer find the main till. Pair them again from the main till and re-check the printer IPs ( Add a device to your main till , checking the link ).

Ready for internet outages Selling carries on — orders, cash payments and receipt printing keep working offline. Everything uploads by itself when the internet returns, never twice ( Working offline ). What truly needs the internet — connected card payments, sending messages, and creating or changing bookings ( What needs the internet ). Keep the router powered — as long as the store Wi-Fi is up, staff-ordering tablets and extra tills keep talking to the main till, and you can even pair new devices ( Pairing devices offline ). Sign in once on every device on install day — offline, only an account that has signed in on that device before can get in ( Signing in offline ).

21 Device modes & customer display Every BrewDesk device has one job. The first device in a shop automatically becomes the main till (Main POS); from the second device on, you pick one of the jobs below. Here they are: Main POS — your main till, and there is only one per shop. To change it in a shop that already has one, use Replace Main POS , which needs an emailed verification code. Sub POS — an extra till to help out ( Register as new device ). You sign in with the owner's email and type a verification code. ( Business plan; up to 3 tills including the main one.) Staff Ordering — your staff take orders from any tablet or phone on your network, and the orders go straight to the main till. ( Pro plan; it shows how many "slots used".) Customer Display — a second screen that shows customers their order. (1 on Pro , up to 3 on Business .) Waitlist Kiosk — a self-check-in screen where walk-in guests add themselves to the waitlist. (This used to be called "Check-in".) Order Kiosk — coming soon. Where to turn it on Staff Ordering and Customer Display are first turned on at the main till, in Settings › Add-ons (Devices section) — Staff Ordering is a Pro add-on. Then register the new device like this: Choose how a device is used This screen was captured on a device where a Main POS is already registered, so the top card is Replace Main POS. ① Replace Main POS · ② Staff Ordering (take orders from any tablet) · ③ Customer Display · ④ Waitlist Kiosk (self check-in for the waitlist). Register as new device, between ① and ②, adds an extra POS (Sub POS). Open the BrewDesk app on the new device and connect it to the same shop Wi-Fi as the main till. On the sign-in screen, tap "Register as a new device at Main POS." A New device pairing request popup appears on the main till. Under Device role pick Staff Ordering, Customer Display or Waitlist Kiosk, then tap Approve . The new device goes straight into the job you picked. The main till chooses the job, not the new device. A new device can't declare "I'm a staff ordering tablet" by itself. See Add a device to your main till for the full steps and what to do if something goes wrong. A device signed in with the owner's email shows a choice screen. "How will you use this device?" lists Replace Main POS , Register as new device , Staff Ordering , Customer Display , Waitlist Kiosk and Order Kiosk (coming soon). Replace Main POS and Register as new device go through an emailed verification code (the first device in a shop automatically becomes the main till); the Staff Ordering, Customer Display and Waitlist Kiosk cards lead into the same main-till approval described above.

Staff Ordering Staff Ordering lets your team take orders from an extra tablet or phone. The orders fly straight to the main till. Here's how to set it up. At the main till, turn on Staff Ordering in Settings › Add-ons (Devices section). It's a Pro add-on. Open the BrewDesk app on the extra tablet or phone and connect it to the same shop Wi-Fi as the main till. On the sign-in screen, tap "Register as a new device at Main POS." In the popup on the main till, under Device role , choose Staff Ordering and Approve . (Pro allows up to 3 Staff Ordering devices, Business has no limit; the registration screen shows "slots used".) Your staff sign in and start taking orders. Each order flows to the main till by itself. (This device has no payment screen and no owner settings — it's just for taking orders.) Great for busy times: staff can take orders right at the table, or walk down a long line so no one waits. Orders always go through your main till. A Staff Ordering tablet hands every order to the main till over your shop Wi-Fi — so it keeps working even when the internet is out, as long as the main till is switched on and on the same network. If it can't reach the main till you'll see Not sent to the kitchen — "Could not reach the Main POS. This order has not reached the kitchen yet." Two buttons: Try again sends it once more (the same order can never go in twice), or Entered on Main POS if you gave up and typed it into the main till yourself. Only tap that second one if you really did — otherwise BrewDesk sends the order again later and it lands twice.

Customer display A customer display is a second screen that faces the customer. It shows them their order and the price as you add things. Here's how to set one up. Where to turn it on Turn it on at the main till in Settings › Add-ons › Customer Display , then pick Customer Display as the job when you register the spare device. Find a spare tablet or screen, open BrewDesk on it, and connect it to the same shop Wi-Fi as the main till. On the sign-in screen, tap "Register as a new device at Main POS." In the popup on the main till, under Device role , choose Customer Display and Approve . The screen joins up with your till by itself. No login needed. Now point the screen toward the customer. As you add items at the till, they show up on this screen too. The Pro plan lets you use 1 display. The Business plan lets you use up to 3. Good to know: a customer display only shows things. It can't take orders or send anything — it just shows the order to your customer.

22 Multiple devices & reliability You can use more than one device at the same time. If one breaks, another one keeps your shop open. Let's set up your devices. Devices ① Main POS (this device) · ② Customer Display switch ( Pro and above) · ③ Disconnect · ④ Note: add devices from the BrewDesk app Sign in with the owner's email on the devices that will be your main till and extra tills. Staff Ordering tablets, customer displays and waitlist kiosks don't use the owner's email sign-in — you approve them at the main till ( Add a device to your main till ). Give each device a job. Pick main till (your number-one device), extra till (a helper device), Staff Ordering , customer display (a screen for customers), or waitlist kiosk . Need to change a device's job later? Ask for the change on that device, then approve it at the main till ( Change a device's job & check the link ). You pick one device as your main till — it's your anchor. It does not hand off on its own. If it ever goes offline, BrewDesk alerts you at once so you can turn it back on or make another device the main till. See Device modes & customer display to set a device's mode, including Staff Ordering. If your main till goes offline. You get told right away — a note in your inbox, an email, and a banner on your other tills. Your other tills keep working, but QR and online orders pause until the main till is back (see QR code ordering ). To make a different device the main till, you switch it yourself and BrewDesk emails you a code to confirm — nothing switches over silently. Give each device a name. In Settings › Devices , tap a device's name (or the little pencil next to it), type something like "Counter 1" or "Bar iPad" , and save. You'll see "Device name updated." The name shows on every device, so you always know which tablet is which. Your tills that connect only over the shop network can't be renamed. Taking the main till off the list? If QR or online ordering is on, BrewDesk warns you first: "This is your Main POS. QR and online ordering are on — while no Main POS is connected, new customer orders can't be taken or printed in the kitchen." It only warns — you can still go ahead. If you can, make another device the main till first. Show this off Your till never dies. Spill a drink on it? Grab any laptop or tablet and you're back in minutes. No special machines, and you're never locked in.

t: Add a device to your main till
b: Add a device to your main till When you add a staff ordering tablet, a customer display, or a waitlist kiosk (self check-in) screen, your main till finds it for you. There is no code to type and no setting to hunt for. It even works when the shop has no internet. What you need The new device must have the BrewDesk app installed (iPad or desktop; the Android app is not available yet), and it must be on the same shop Wi-Fi as your main till. A page opened in a web browser can't be registered as a device — you'll see "Add devices from the BrewDesk app" instead. New device looking for the Main POS (not found) ① "Register as a new device at Main POS" screen · ② Try again · ③ Back to sign in The "New device pairing request" popup on the main POS (sample screen) ① Device name and IP address · ② Device role — pick its job · ③ Deny · ④ Approve Open the BrewDesk app on the new device. On the sign-in screen, tap "Register as a new device at Main POS." If the device has no internet, it goes to this screen on its own. You'll see "Looking for Main POS..." and then the request is sent automatically. There is nothing more to tap on the new device — just leave it on "Waiting for approval at the Main POS." A popup called New device pairing request appears on your main till by itself. It shows which device asked, with its name and address. Under Device role , pick what this device is for — Staff Ordering , Customer Display , or Waitlist Kiosk (self check-in). The approve button stays off until you pick one. Tap Approve . If you don't recognise the device, tap Deny . The new device shows New device registration complete and goes straight into the job you picked for it. You choose the job, not the new device. A new device can't tell your till "I'm a staff ordering tablet." Only the person standing at the main till picks the job — so a tablet someone quietly plugs in can't decide for itself what it's allowed to do. This never makes a main till. Your main till is always set up by signing in with your email, and BrewDesk emails you a code to confirm when you change it. Extra tills (Sub POS) are also registered by signing in with email and confirming a code. Says "Couldn't find the Main POS"? Usually the two devices are on different Wi-Fi. Connect to the shop Wi-Fi — not guest Wi-Fi and not a phone hotspot — then tap Try again . If the popup sits too long you'll see Request expired ; just start again from the new device. On the main till, Settings › Devices now shows a How to add a device guide instead of register buttons — registering always starts on the new device.

t: Change a device's job & check the link
b: Change a device's job & check the link You can change what an already-paired device does, or check whether it's still talking to your main till. On a Staff Ordering device, tap the device mode icon ("Switch device mode") at the top of the screen. Change device role opens. You don't need a code again — this device is already registered. Pick the new job — Staff Ordering (take orders from any device), Customer Display (show orders to customers), or Waitlist Kiosk (self check-in for the waitlist). Nothing changes on the tablet yet. It says "Waiting for Main POS approval" — "Ask the owner to approve this change on the Main POS screen. Nothing has changed on this device yet." Go to your main till . A card pops up by itself, tagged "Role change — existing device" : "This device is already registered and is asking to change its role. Approving changes what it does; its login is not affected." Tap Approve — or Deny if you didn't expect it. The tablet then switches. At the top of that window you'll see the link status. Connected to the main POS means all is well. No main POS connected means it hasn't found it yet — tap Check again . To remove this device completely, tap Log out & unregister at the bottom. It returns to the sign-in screen, and after signing back in you can choose its job from scratch. When something looks wrong — Connection log . Tap the connection log icon at the top of the screen to see, on one page, which shop and job this device is registered to, how long it has been linked to the main till, and how many orders haven't been sent up yet. When you contact support, Copy all and paste it in — that's the fastest way to get help. Changing a device's job now needs your approval. Whoever is holding the tablet can ask , but only the main till can say yes — so a guest or a passer-by can't quietly turn your kiosk into an ordering device. The request expires after 2 minutes ("This request expires in {seconds}s — approve now or ask the device to send a new one"); if it runs out, just ask again from the tablet. Turning a device into a Sub POS asks twice. A Sub POS can take money, so the main till warns you first — "This device will be able to take payments." / "A Sub POS can ring up orders, take payment and issue refunds. Approve only a device you set up yourself." Tap Continue to confirm. If you don't recognise the device, tap Deny .

t: When you hit the device limit
b: When you hit the device limit Your plan includes a certain number of tills and customer displays. When you reach that number, BrewDesk doesn't just refuse — it offers you a straight swap of one device for another. Where to find it Settings › Devices shows a warning strip at the top as soon as you reach the limit (not only when you go over it), counting what you're using — for example POS 1/1 and Customer display 1/1 on Pro , or POS 3/3 and Customer display 3/3 on Business . Each device also shows Last seen , so you can tell which one has been sitting in a drawer. Register the new till as usual. If you're at the limit you'll see "You've reached your plan's device limit. Replace an existing device, or upgrade your plan to add more." A Replace a device picker opens, listing the devices you could retire. Pick one. That's it — the old device is disconnected and the new one takes its place on the spot. Changed nothing on that list for a while? If the device you picked was already disconnected you'll see "That device was already disconnected, or this list is out of date — refreshing the list." Pick again from the fresh list. Your main till is never in that list. Replacing the main till is a bigger deal, so it has its own route: the Replace Main POS card, which confirms and emails you a code first. The quick swap above is only for the extra devices. We email you too. On the web, when a device is turned away for hitting the limit, BrewDesk emails the store owner as well — the message says "We've also emailed the store owner about this." So if a member of staff hits this at 7am, you find out without them having to explain it. Staff Ordering has its own count. Pro includes 3 Staff Ordering slots (Business has no limit). Run out of slots and the registration screen tells you plainly: "All 3 Staff Ordering slots are in use (3/3). Release a device in Settings → Devices to add another." If your plan doesn't include it at all: "Staff Ordering isn't included in your current plan." On an iPad or the desktop app the wording is slightly shorter and points you to your BrewDesk account on the web to change your plan — the swap itself works exactly the same.

23 Receipts & printers BrewDesk can print receipts for customers and tickets for the kitchen. Let's add a printer step by step. And if a printer ever jams, your order is still safe. Printers ① Add Printer · ② A connected printer card (status, role, Test) · ③ Setup Guide · ④ Print Log Add Printer — fill it in top to bottom ① Printer Name · ② Connection (USB or Wi-Fi/LAN) · ③ IP Address (for Wi-Fi) · ④ Printer Role (Main Receipt / Kitchen / None) · ⑤ Add Printer Printer list & Print Log ① Add Printer · ② Test · ③ In Use switch · ④ Print Log filter (All / Success / Failed) · ⑤ Failed job — Retry · Check Network Open Settings › Printers . You'll see Connected Printers and the buttons Add USB Printer , Add Wi-Fi Printer , and Add Printer . Tap Add Wi-Fi Printer (or Add USB Printer ). The printer window opens. Type a Printer Name , like "Kitchen Printer", so you can tell your printers apart. Pick a Connection Type — USB or Wi-Fi/LAN. For Wi-Fi: type the printer's IP Address (like 192.168.1.50) and Port (usually 9100), then tap Connect . If you only know part of the IP, tap Search to scan for it. For USB: under Select installed printer , tap Load printers and pick your printer from the list. (The BrewDesk desktop app must be running, and the printer must be installed in your OS to appear in the list.) Add Printer — lower part ① Load printers · ② Printer Role · ③ Print Copies · ④ Paper Width · ⑤ Cash Drawer · ⑥ Add Printer Choose the Printer Role : Main Receipt (customer receipts), Kitchen (kitchen tickets) or None (no role). If it's a Kitchen printer, pick a Kitchen Print Mode : Whole Order (one ticket per order) or Per Item (a ticket per item). Set Print Copies if you want more than one copy. Tap Test Print to print a test page, then tap Add Printer to save it. Tax-inclusive shop? The tax line now says so. If your prices already include tax, the receipt and the bill print the tax line with "incl." after the label. The amount hasn't changed and neither has the total — it's there so nobody adds the tax line on top of the items and thinks the total is wrong. It was always included; now the paper says it. Text getting cut off, or non-English characters printing as gibberish? Open "Printing looks wrong?" near the bottom of the printer window and tap Print test receipt . A sample prints, and you just answer two things by looking at it — ① "Which block looked clean?" (pick the one where lines didn't wrap onto the next line), and ② which of lines [A] and [B] you can actually read. No numbers to look up — you just pick what looks right. Good to know: 80mm printers now default to 42 characters a line, which suits most printers — if your receipts look fine, leave this alone. If neither block looks right, choose Enter number and type the number from the ruler at the bottom of the test receipt (20–96). "No print confirmation" on a Wi-Fi printer. Some Wi-Fi printers can't tell BrewDesk whether paper really came out. Their card shows a grey note: No print confirmation — "This printer can't report whether paper came out. A ticket that fails to print won't be flagged." When you tap Test Print , you'll see "Test page sent. This printer can't confirm printing — check that paper came out." So look at the printer yourself. It's not a fault — your printer just can't report back. Don't know your printer's IP address? No problem. Tap Search and BrewDesk looks across your network for it. Wi-Fi printers usually use port 9100 — if you're unsure, leave it as is. On an iPad? Printing works right inside the app — no browser helper needed. Just add your Wi-Fi / LAN printer the same way (tap Search to find it), or use an AirPrint printer. No kitchen printer? That's fine. If you don't have one set up, BrewDesk simply skips kitchen tickets. Nothing breaks. One printer for both jobs? If a single printer prints both receipts and kitchen tickets (combined mode), you can still turn on Per Item so each item gets its own kitchen ticket — handy when one machine does everything. Everyday printing. Once a printer is saved, receipts print when you take payment, and kitchen tickets print when you send an order to the kitchen. Need another copy? Open the order and tap Reprint . If a print ever fails, it waits in a list — just tap Retry . The order is never lost. USB printer — use the installed driver (recommended) This is the easy way. Install your printer's driver the normal way (Mac is usually automatic; Windows uses the manufacturer driver), open the BrewDesk desktop app , then in Settings › Printers › "Add USB Printer" choose Select installed printer › Load printers and pick it. Wi-Fi / LAN printers don't need this process either.

Order & queue numbers In counter service, every order gets a number. It's great for calling out "now serving number A-005!" so customers know when their drink is ready. Here's how to set it up and show it on the receipt. Open Settings › Tables and find the Counter Mode options. Turn on Auto Order Number so every order gets its own number. Set a Number Prefix if you like — for example A-001 . Turn on Daily Reset to restart the count each day, so you begin fresh every morning. The number prints on the receipt as the order number — for example "ORDER: #TX-ORD-1042" . What's the order number for? It's the easy way to match a finished drink to the right customer — you call the number instead of a name. You can also design what your receipts look like in Settings › Receipts . There are tabs for Receipt , Kitchen , and Queue Number , Waitlist Ticket . Drag blocks to show or hide things like a big Queue Number , a custom message, a refund policy, a loyalty stamp, or a QR code. The live preview on the right shows exactly how it will print. Want the number nice and big? Turn on the Queue Number block in the receipt builder. The preview on the right updates as you change things, so you always see how the printed receipt will look. Receipt builder ① Receipt / Kitchen / Queue Number / Waitlist Ticket tabs · ② Show / hide switch for the Queue Number block · ③ The order number on the receipt (#TX-ORD-1042) · ④ Save Designing the kitchen ticket ① Kitchen tab · ② Block list — tap to show or hide · ③ Preview · ④ 58mm / Save Designing the waitlist ticket ① Waitlist Ticket tab · ② Block list · ③ Preview · ④ Test Print · ⑤ Reset

24 Going live Here is how to move from practice mode to real trading. You start in practice mode . Tap anything, ring up pretend orders — none of it counts as real takings. When you're ready to actually trade, you switch to live . Where to find it While you're in practice mode there's a strip across the top of the screen: "Practice mode — sales are not counted as real revenue" . Tap Go Live next to it. Practice mode band ① "Practice mode" band (sales are not counted as real revenue) · ② Go Live button Do it on the main till. Going live can only be done from your main register: "Only the main POS can switch the store to live. Open this on your main register."

Fill in the checklist Go-live checklist ① A required setting still missing · ② Set up — jump to that setting · ③ Re-check If anything's still missing, a checklist appears first — store name, country, currency, timezone, business type, confirmed tax rate, tax ID, store address, and at least one menu item. Tap Set up on a line to jump straight to that setting. When you've filled them in, tap Re-check . Why block it? If you start trading with your tax rate or timezone still blank, your first day's takings get recorded wrong — and that's much more painful to fix afterwards. So we ask you to confirm it once, up front.

Choose how to start Going live — choose how to start (this shot shows options A and B) ① Keep sandbox (Still practicing) · ② Reset & start — erase practice data and start live Then pick one of three — Still practicing (carry on practising, nothing changes), Reset and go live (wipe the practice records and start clean), or Already in business (keep everything you've rung up so far, and tell us which day you actually opened). You get one more confirmation screen listing exactly what gets deleted and what stays. For the two real options BrewDesk emails you a code to type in — going live is a one-way door, so we check it's really you. Done. Your sales now count officially, and customers can order from their phones. Already taken real money? Then "Still practicing" disappears. If BrewDesk can see real orders, real card payments or closed days on your account, that card is hidden and it says so: "Real sales detected — 'Keep practicing' is not available. Choose Reset (B) or Keep data & go live (C)." A panel shows you what it found — how many orders, how much, whether cards were used. Pretending yesterday's real takings were practice is how books stop balancing. Your menu, tax, printers, staff and Stripe settings all stay. Even if you choose "Reset & start", the only things removed are the practice orders, sales and closing records. Good to know: while you're in practice mode, customers can't place real QR or online orders. Their screen says "This store is in practice mode".

26 Troubleshooting & support Things go wrong sometimes — that's okay. Here are quick fixes for the most common ones, and how to ask us for help. Profile icon (D) menu — where to refresh ① Profile & Account · ② Check for updates — check for the newest version and refresh Support ① Create New Ticket · ② Start your first ticket The Card button looks grey and won't tap? You haven't linked your Stripe account yet. Go to Getting paid to connect it. The internet went out? Don't worry — just keep selling. BrewDesk works fine offline. See Working offline . A kitchen ticket didn't print? Check the printer is on, then look in the retry list. See Receipts & printers . A blank white screen, or the app looks stuck after an update? Tap the Refresh / Clear cache button at the top of the screen and confirm. It clears the old app files and loads a fresh copy — your saved orders and settings are safe. Create a support ticket ① Type · ② Subject · ③ Message · ④ Submit Still stuck? In the app, go to Settings › Support › Create New Ticket to open a support ticket (that means you write us a message). Or go to brewdesk.io. Refresh / Clear cache is the quick fix right after an update. It reloads the newest version of the app without touching your saved orders or settings. A support ticket is just a message you send to our help team. Tell us what went wrong and we'll get back to you. Buttons cut off, or text too small on a little tablet? Open the account menu (top right) and look for Display Scaling . Leave it on Auto and BrewDesk fits the screen to your device by itself, showing you the percentage it picked. Switch to Manual if you'd rather choose the size yourself. Not signed in, or helping someone who isn't? There's a plain help page at brewdesk.io/support — no login needed. It has our email address, how long we usually take to reply, and answers to the questions we get most (offline, hardware, card payments, device limits, cancelling, where your data lives).

Automatic updates We improve BrewDesk all the time, and your till picks up the new version by itself. It never does that in the middle of a sale — here's exactly when it happens and what you'll see. Updates only start just after you switch the till on for the day — not while you're using it. A page refresh doesn't count; it has to be a real restart. Even then BrewDesk checks it's safe first: the basket must be empty , no payment in progress, you're online, and nothing is waiting to sync. If any of that isn't true, it waits for another day. You get a 3-second warning before anything happens: "Starting the update" → "Starting in 3s." Not now? Just touch the screen. The message says "Tap the screen to do this later" — one tap cancels it and you carry on. It won't ask again until the next time you switch on. If you let it run, the update screen appears with your logo and a short line telling you what it's doing: "Checking the new version" → "Loading the screen" → "Loading your store" . It only happens once a day per device. It tells you when it's taking a while. After about 15 seconds the line changes to "Taking a little longer. You can leave it as is." Nothing is broken — leave it alone and it will finish. In a hurry? Start with what's saved. If it's still waiting after roughly 22 seconds you'll see "Waiting for your store information" and a Start with saved data button. Tap it and you go straight into your store screen using the information already on the device, so you can serve the next customer. You never have to sit and watch it. The bottom of the screen always says "When the update finishes, it'll return to your store screen on its own." And if the update can't finish, BrewDesk gives up rather than trapping you: "We skipped the update this time. Everything works just as before." Updating on purpose — and why it sometimes waits You can also ask for the update yourself instead of waiting for the next morning. A list opens showing what's new, with an update button underneath. Update check result ① Message and current version · ② OK Tap the update button. If the till is busy, nothing is lost — BrewDesk holds the update and tells you why in one line. "An order is still open. We'll apply it once it's done." — finish or park the basket. "A payment is in progress. We'll apply it when it's done." — never mid-payment, ever. "Please check your internet connection." or "Some orders haven't been sent yet. We'll apply it once they're synced." — it waits until your orders are safely up. When the coast is clear it says "Getting the new version" and then reloads your store screen by itself. Taking its time? After about 20 seconds you'll see "Taking a little longer. You can leave it as is." If it really can't fetch it: "We couldn't get the new version right now. Please try again in a moment." Nothing is broken and nothing is lost — carry on serving and try later. After it updates, it tells you. Next time the till starts you get a short note — "This version includes improvements and fixes." — so a screen that looks slightly different isn't a mystery.
27 FAQ The questions staff, owners and installers ask most often. The answers are kept short — follow the link at the end of each one for the full steps.

Getting started, plans & account Do I need a credit card or special hardware to start? No. You sign up with an email and password, and BrewDesk runs on the laptop or tablet you already have. The Pro and Business free trials don't need a credit card to start either. → Quick start · Welcome & overview How do I clear out the orders I rang up while practising? When you go live, choose Reset and go live (wipe the practice records and start clean). Only the practice orders, sales and closing records are removed — your menu, tax, printers, staff and Stripe settings all stay. → Choose how to start How do I change plan, or stop after the free trial? Your plan, payment card and invoices are all under Billing . If you don't want to carry on after the trial, simply don't add a card — you can keep using the free Starter plan. In the iPad and desktop apps, change your plan from your BrewDesk account on the web. → Your plan & billing I asked to delete my account — can I take it back? Yes. Deletion only happens after 14 days. Until then, sign in again and tap Cancel deletion at the top of the screen and it's as if you never asked. No code is needed, and the owner or a manager can cancel it. → Deleting your account How do I turn on extras like QR ordering or Staff? Go to Settings › Add-ons and tap the switch on the card. Free add-ons work on every plan; some (Online Ordering/QR, Loyalty, Staff, Scheduler and others) come with the Pro plan; text messages (SMS) are pay-as-you-go. → Turn add-ons on and off

Payments, refunds & closing What are the card fees? BrewDesk adds 0% to your card sales, on every plan. The money goes straight into your own Stripe account; the only fee is Stripe's standard fee, which you pay to Stripe directly. Linking Stripe is free on every plan. → Getting paid The Card button is grey and won't tap. You haven't linked your Stripe account yet. Connect it in Settings › Payments . Cards taken on a separate terminal can still be recorded with the card-brand buttons or Card (External) . → Getting paid Can staff give refunds? A refund only goes through once a manager approves it with their PIN, so a staff member can't do it alone. The owner decides which roles may refund in Settings › Staff Permissions . → Refunds · Permissions, manager PIN & role chip I forgot to close the day. Next time you open BrewDesk, an Unclosed Business Days window lists the missed dates, and new sales pause until they're closed. The easy choice is Auto-Close All ; to check each day yourself, choose Close One by One . → Late orders & missed days A payment came in after I closed the day. The payment goes through as normal, then you'll see Additional Closing Needed . Review and close, and BrewDesk saves it as a separate additional closing report — the original Z-Report never changes. → Late orders & missed days The Close Day button is greyed out. A cash drawer session is still open, or there are unpaid orders left. Use Open drawer next to the message to count the cash and end the session, or settle or cancel the open orders, then close again. → Cash drawer

Devices, internet & printers What happens if the internet goes down? Keep taking orders, cash payments and printing receipts as usual. Orders are saved on the device and upload by themselves when the internet returns — never twice. Only connected card-reader payments, sending messages, and creating or changing bookings have to wait. → Working offline · What needs the internet Receipts or kitchen tickets aren't printing. Check the printer is on; failed prints wait in a list, so just tap Retry . Some Wi-Fi printers show No print confirmation and can't report a failure, so check the paper with your eyes. Need another copy? Open the order and tap Reprint . → Receipts & printers How many devices can I connect? It depends on the plan. Tills (including the main one): Starter and Pro 1, Business 3. Customer displays: Pro 1, Business 3. Staff ordering devices: Pro 3, Business unlimited. When you hit the limit, BrewDesk offers Replace a device to swap one out. → When you hit the device limit QR orders aren't reaching the till. QR orders come in through the main till, so if it's off or offline, new QR orders pause. While the internet is down, don't issue new table QR codes — take orders by hand instead. And in practice mode, guests can't place real QR orders at all. → Running it day to day · Going live If the main till goes off, does the shop stop? No. The other tills keep working, and BrewDesk tells you straight away — inbox alert, email and a banner on the other tills. QR and online orders do pause until the main till is back, and making another device the main till is something the owner does by hand, with an email code. → Multiple devices & reliability

Staff, PINs & data A staff member forgot their PIN. Open that person in Settings › Staff Permissions › Staff and tap "Reset to 0000" . The owner or a manager can do it. Nobody can sign in with 0000, so have them set a new PIN straight away. → Forgot a PIN? I forgot the owner PIN or the manager PIN. For the owner PIN, tap "Forgot your PIN?" in the role chip panel and set a new one with the 6-digit code sent to your sign-up email. For the manager PIN, the owner simply sets a new one on the manager PIN card in Settings › Staff Permissions . → Forgot a PIN? How do I back up my store's data? On the backup page in Settings, tap Connect Google Drive to link your own Drive; from then on BrewDesk keeps saving new backups by itself. To get an older copy, tap Restore and pick one. For files to hand your accountant, use Accounting Export in Closing History. → Backups · Export your sales Question not here? Type a word in the search box at the top, or see Troubleshooting & support for how to open a support ticket.

Orders travel over the store Wi-Fi to the Main POS. Pro 3 devices, Business unlimited. → Staff Ordering Customer Display A screen turned towards the customer showing the order and prices. It can't be undone. → Going live Hold Parks an unpaid order so you can reopen it later. → Hold an order Quick discount · Free item A one-off price cut or giveaway made at the till, recorded with a reason chip. Free items are counted separately from discounts at closing. → Quick discount or free item Record Only payment A way to just record a card payment taken on a separate terminal that isn't connected to BrewDesk. Shown as card-brand buttons (Visa, MasterCard and so on) or Card (External) on the payment screen. → Getting paid Split · Split Pay Split divides one bill between several people, evenly or by item; Split Pay lets one person pay with several methods, such as cash + card. → Split the bill Cash Payment Rounding Rounds cash totals to the smallest coin actually in use. Closing & cash Term Meaning Close Day Wrapping up the day and locking in its totals.
